definition_zh: 原则上、理论上；大体上（表示道理上成立，但实际未必照此实行）
definition_en: as a matter of theory or general rule; in the main, though practice may differ
core_image: 图纸上画出一条笔直的线，工地上却要绕开一块巨石
scene: 设计图上那条通道可以直穿山体，施工队到了现场才发现岩层太硬，只能改走侧坡。 In principle the tunnel could be driven straight through, but the rock refused.
sceneCN: 这里取「原则上、理论上」（第 1 个义项：道理上可行，实际未必）；句意为原则上隧道可以直穿过去，但岩层不允许。

pos.zh: 副词短语：原则上；理论上；大体上

forms.label: 对照形式
forms.form: in principle but not in practice

derivatives.zh: 主要的；校长（同根不同义）

senses.title: True in theory
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible or correct as a matter of theory, whether or not it happens
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事在道理上可行或正确，不论实际是否发生
senses.example: In principle, the two networks can be linked.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上，这两个网络可以互联。
senses.why: A principle is a starting point, and from a starting point a conclusion may follow without being carried out.
senses.whyCN: 原则是起点，从起点可以推出结论，却未必真的去做。

senses.title: Beside theory talk
senses.titleCN: 近义辨析：与理论说法相近
senses.definition: it resembles the phrase about theory, though it points to a rule or a foundation rather than to a model
senses.definitionCN: 它与表理论的说法相近，只是指向规则或根基，而非模型
senses.example: In principle the method is sound; in practice it is too slow.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法在理论上站得住；实际做起来太慢。
senses.why: Theory suggests a model of how things work, while principle suggests a rule that governs them.
senses.whyCN: 理论暗示事物运作的模型，原则暗示支配事物的规则。

senses.title: Not on principle
senses.definition: the phrase states what is possible in theory, while the look-alike with on states what a person refuses or accepts on moral grounds
senses.definitionCN: 这个短语陈述理论上可能的事，而形近短语陈述某人基于道义理由拒绝或接受什么
senses.example: In principle she accepted the rule, though she disliked it.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上她接受了这条规定，尽管并不喜欢。
senses.why: One frame is about feasibility, the other about conviction, and the prepositions keep them apart.
senses.whyCN: 一个框架谈可行性，另一个谈信念，介词把两者分开。

senses.title: Agreement with a reserve
senses.titleCN: 会议义：原则同意但留保留
senses.definition: in committee language it records approval of an idea while details or costs remain to be settled
senses.definitionCN: 在委员会语言中，记录对想法的认可，而细节或费用仍待敲定
senses.example: The board agreed in principle to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会原则上同意这次合并。
senses.why: Approval of a principle is cheaper than approval of a budget, which is why the phrase is so useful in meetings.
senses.whyCN: 认可一项原则比批准一笔预算便宜，因此这个短语在会议上十分好用。

senses.title: A rule of law or policy
senses.titleCN: 原则义：法律与政策准则
senses.definition: it can state that a right or a duty exists as a general rule, subject to conditions
senses.definitionCN: 可说明某项权利或义务作为通则存在，但须受条件限制
senses.example: In principle, every citizen may apply for the grant.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上，每位公民都可以申请这项补助。
senses.why: A general rule covers everyone on paper, and conditions decide what happens in fact.
senses.whyCN: 通则在纸面上覆盖所有人，条件决定事实上如何。

senses.title: The level of a law of nature
senses.definition: in science it marks what follows from a law or a mechanism, before engineering limits are counted
senses.definitionCN: 在科学中，标出由定律或机理推出的事，尚未计入工程限制
senses.example: In principle the reaction releases energy at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上该反应在室温下就释放能量。
senses.why: A mechanism may allow something that a real apparatus cannot deliver, and the phrase keeps that gap open.
senses.whyCN: 机理允许的事，真实装置未必做得到，这个短语把那个差距留着。

senses.title: Concession, then caveat
senses.titleCN: 让步义：先认可再提条件
senses.definition: it concedes the general case before the speaker adds a condition or a cost
senses.definitionCN: 先承认一般情形，随后补上条件或代价
senses.example: The plan is acceptable in principle, subject to cost review.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案原则上可以接受，但须视成本评审而定。
senses.why: The frame makes a concession sound generous while keeping a door open for refusal.
senses.whyCN: 这个框架让让步显得大度，同时为拒绝留着一扇门。

senses.title: Not the head of a school
senses.titleCN: 辨义：不表校长或负责人
senses.definition: the related adjective and noun can name a school head, but the phrase states feasibility only
senses.definitionCN: 相关形容词与名词可指校长，但短语只陈述可行性
senses.example: In principle marks a theoretical stand, not a school head.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上这一说法标的是理论立场，不是学校校长。
senses.why: English split the two spellings, and only the noun with the narrower meaning entered this phrase.
senses.whyCN: 英语把两种拼写分了工，只有词义较窄的那个名词进入了这个短语。

intro.en: Principle comes from Latin principium, a beginning or foundation, from princeps, first or chief, built on primus, first, and capere, to take. The Latin chain is secure; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: principle 出自拉丁语 principium「开端、基础」，源于 princeps「居首者」，由 primus「第一」与 capere「取」构成。拉丁语链条清楚；短语属近代。

items.en: Primus meant first in order, and it stands behind primary and prime as well.
items.cn: primus 意为次序上的第一，也支撑着 primary 与 prime 等词。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and its compounds cover capture, reception and acceptance.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓取，其复合词涵盖捕获、接收与接受。

items.en: The compound named the one who takes the first place, hence a chief or a leader.
items.cn: 这个复合词指占据首位的人，因此指首领。

items.en: The noun moved from a beginning in time to a foundation on which reasoning rests.
items.cn: 这个名词从时间上的开端转为推理所依托的基础。

items.en: English keeps principle for a rule and principal for a chief or a school head.
items.cn: 英语用前者指原则，用后者指首领或校长。

items.en: The theoretical qualifier belongs to modern discussion; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个理论性限定语属于近代讨论，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the form or the root but means a rule, a refusal or a head; the second group are phrases of theory and feasibility.
note.cn: 第一组共用形式或词根，却指规则、拒绝或负责人；第二组是表理论与可行性的短语。

entries.definition: It means because of a conviction, not because something is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 意为出于信念，而非因为某事可行。

entries.definition: The look-alike noun names a person or a main sum.
entries.definitionCN: 形近名词指负责人或本金。

entries.definition: It contrasts a model with actual practice.
entries.definitionCN: 把模型与实际做法相对。

entries.definition: It names what really happens, the usual partner of the frame.
entries.definitionCN: 它指真正发生的情况，常与本短语配对。

entries.definition: A single adverb for what follows from theory.
entries.definitionCN: 由理论推出的单词副词。

entries.definition: It means as recorded or planned, before reality tests it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为按记录或计划，尚未经现实检验。

entries.definition: It states what normally happens, not what is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述通常发生的事，而非可能的事。

entries.definition: It marks a statement made at a general level.
entries.definitionCN: 标出在一般层面作出的陈述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-taker root, the split between principle and principal, and the real pairing with practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的居首取位词根、原则与校长的分工，以及与实践的真实配对。

normal.en: The root is the first taker, so a principle is where reasoning starts.
normal.cn: 词根是居首取位者，因此原则是推理起步之处。

normal.en: Two spellings split the work: a rule on one side, a chief on the other.
normal.cn: 两种拼写分担功能：一边是规则，一边是首领。

normal.en: Theory gives a model, while principle gives a governing rule.
normal.cn: 理论给出模型，原则给出支配规则。

normal.en: The phrase usually faces its partner, practice, across a semicolon.
normal.cn: 这个短语常与搭档「实践」隔一个分号相望。

normal.en: In meetings it records approval of an idea before the bill arrives.
normal.cn: 在会议上，它在账单到来前先记下对想法的认可。

abstract.en: Like a straight line drawn on a plan, before the boulder on site is seen.
abstract.cn: 像图纸上画的直线，工地上的巨石尚未看见。

abstract.en: Like a rule written at the top of a page, with conditions pencilled below.
abstract.cn: 像写在页首的规则，条件用铅笔注在下面。

abstract.en: Like a door marked open on a map, which may still be locked in fact.
abstract.cn: 像地图上标着开启的门，实际上可能仍锁着。

examples.en: In principle, the two systems can share one database.
examples.cn: 原则上，两个系统可以共用一个数据库。

examples.en: The committee approved the idea in principle.
examples.cn: 委员会原则上同意了这个想法。

examples.en: In principle the repair is simple, though it needs a crane.
examples.cn: 原则上这次修理很简单，只是需要一台吊车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 普林塞泼」——图纸上的直线，工地上的巨石：原则上

root: 核心名词意为原则，出自拉丁语 principium「开端、基础」，源于 princeps「居首者」，由 primus「第一」与 capere「取」构成。该短语表原则上为近代用法，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate feasibility in theory, the near twin about theory, the contrast with a moral stance, committee approval with a reserve, legal and policy rules, scientific mechanism, concession with a condition, and the exclusion of a school head.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项区分：理论可行性、与理论说的近义辨析、与道义立场的对照、会议中的保留式同意、法律政策准则、科学机理、带条件的让步，以及排除校长义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn on a plan, while a boulder on the site forces a detour.
core.cn: 核心意象：图纸上画出的一条直线，而工地上的巨石逼出一条绕行。

branches.en: THE THEORY: what follows from a rule or a mechanism before limits are counted.
branches.cn: 理论：由规则或机理推出的事，尚未计入限制。

branches.en: THE NEAR TWIN: a model of how things work differs from a rule that governs them.
branches.cn: 近义辨析：事物运作的模型不同于支配它们的规则。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: feasibility is not a moral conviction.
branches.cn: 对照：可行性不同于道义信念。

branches.en: THE RESERVE: approval of an idea can be given before details or costs are settled.
branches.cn: 保留：在细节或费用敲定前先认可想法。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE LIMIT: general rights are stated, and no school head is meant.
branches.cn: 规则与边界：陈述普遍权利，且不指校长。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin noun of beginning and foundation built from the words for first and to take.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个表开端与基础的拉丁语名词上，该名词由「第一」与「取」两个词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus, first, plus capere, to take, gave princeps, the first taker, and principium, a beginning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus「第一」加 capere「取」，给出 princeps「居首取位者」与 principium「开端」。

items.example: The adjective supplies the first element.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供第一个成分。

items.example: The verb supplies the second element.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供第二个成分。

items.example: The compound names the one who takes first place.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指占据首位的人。

items.example: The noun shifts from time to reasoning.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从时间转向推理。

items.meaning: a rule; a law of nature
items.example: English narrows it to a governing rule.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它收窄为支配性规则。

items.example: The doublet kept the personal and the leading senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个同源异形词保留人身与首要两义。

items.example: The suffix marks a person who follows a rule.
items.exampleCN: 后缀标出依规则行事的人。

items.example: The negative prefix removes the rule.
The other frame marks a moral ground.
items.exampleCN: 另一个框架标出道义依据。

items.example: The frame is standard in feasibility talk.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架是可行性讨论的标准形式。

definition_zh: 细胞膜；质膜；包裹细胞质的磷脂双分子层
definition_en: the thin barrier of lipid and protein that surrounds a cell and controls what enters or leaves
core_image: 显微镜下一枚细胞被荧光勾出细边，染料在边外停住
scene: 显微镜下，一枚细胞被荧光勾出细细的边，染料在边外停住。 The cell membrane lets water through but keeps most dyes outside.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（细胞膜）；句意为细胞膜允许水通过，却把大多数染料挡在外面。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁表示「皮、膜」的名词构成，义为「膜；薄膜」
由「膜」加形容词词尾构成，义为「膜的；膜状的」
由拉丁表示「小室」的名词构成，义为「细胞；小室」
由「细胞」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞的；多孔的」
由表示「在下、次级」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚细胞的」
由表示「在内」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「细胞内的」

senses.title: The boundary of a cell
senses.definition: the outer boundary separating the cytoplasm from the surrounding medium
senses.definitionCN: 指把细胞质与周围介质隔开的外边界
senses.example: Every cell membrane separates inside from outside.
senses.exampleCN: 每一层细胞膜都把内与外分开。
senses.why: A cell is a room, and a room needs a wall; the phrase names that wall.
senses.whyCN: 细胞是一间屋子，屋子需要墙，这条短语说的就是那面墙。

senses.title: The phospholipid bilayer
senses.definition: the double sheet of lipid molecules with their heads outward and tails inward
senses.definitionCN: 指脂质分子头朝外、尾朝内排成的双层薄片
senses.example: The cell membrane is a bilayer only a few nanometres thick.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜是仅几纳米厚的双分子层。
senses.why: The barrier is not solid but a double layer of molecules, which explains its fluid behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这层屏障并非实心，而是分子的双层，这解释了它的流动性。

senses.title: A selectively permeable barrier
senses.definition: the property of admitting some substances while excluding others
senses.definitionCN: 指允许某些物质通过、同时排斥另一些物质的性质
senses.example: The cell membrane is selectively permeable to ions.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜对离子具有选择性通透。
senses.why: The wall is picky: small neutral molecules pass, charged ones usually need help.
senses.whyCN: 这面墙很挑剔：小的中性分子能过，带电的通常需要帮助。

senses.title: The site of transport proteins
senses.definition: the place where channels, pumps and carriers move substances across
senses.definitionCN: 指通道、泵与载体把物质运送过去的地方
senses.example: Ion channels in the cell membrane open in response to a signal.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜中的离子通道会响应信号而开启。
senses.why: Because the lipid layer rejects charge, proteins must supply the doors.
senses.whyCN: 脂质层排斥电荷，因此必须由蛋白质提供门。

senses.title: A signalling interface
senses.definition: the surface where receptors detect hormones, signals or neighbouring cells
senses.definitionCN: 指受体探测激素、信号或邻近细胞的表面
senses.example: Receptors on the cell membrane detect the hormone.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜上的受体探测这种激素。
senses.why: A cell must listen before it acts, and the membrane is its ear.
senses.whyCN: 细胞要先听再行动，而细胞膜就是它的耳朵。

senses.title: A shape-giving and anchoring layer
senses.titleCN: 维持形状与锚定的结构层
senses.definition: the layer that gives the cell shape and anchors its internal skeleton and proteins
senses.definitionCN: 指赋予细胞形状、并锚定内部骨架与蛋白的层次
senses.example: The cell membrane anchors the fibres that hold its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜锚定维持形状的纤维。
senses.why: A thin skin can still organise everything attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 一层薄膜仍能组织起附着在它上面的一切。

senses.title: A structure compared across cell types
senses.titleCN: 不同细胞类型间的结构比较
senses.definition: the membrane as it appears in bacteria, archaea, plants or animals, with different lipids and additions
senses.definitionCN: 指细菌、古菌、植物或动物细胞中因脂质与附加结构不同而呈现的膜
senses.example: The bacterial cell membrane lacks the cholesterol found in animals.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌细胞膜缺少动物细胞中的胆固醇。
senses.why: The same barrier is built differently in different branches of life, and comparison reveals which parts are essential.
senses.whyCN: 同一道屏障在不同生命分支里造法不同，比较便能显出哪些部件必不可少。

senses.title: A model and a drug target
senses.definition: an artificial or studied membrane used to test transport, or a target for medicines
senses.definitionCN: 指用于测试运输的人工或研究对象膜，或药物作用的靶点
senses.example: Many drugs act on the cell membrane rather than inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多药物作用于细胞膜而非细胞内部。
senses.why: If the boundary is where signals arrive, it is also the easiest place to interrupt them.
senses.whyCN: 若边界是信号到达之处，它也是最容易拦截信号的地方。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room or store, and English applied it to the units of living tissue in the seventeenth century. Membrane comes from Latin membrana, a skin or parchment, generally said to derive from membrum, a limb. The compound cell membrane belongs to nineteenth-century microscopy.
intro.cn: 「细胞」出自拉丁语 cella「小室、储藏间」，英语在十七世纪把它用于活组织的单位。「膜」出自拉丁语 membrana「皮、羊皮纸」，一般认为来自 membrum「肢体」。这条合成短语属于十九世纪的显微观察传统。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 这个词意为小室、储藏间或神庙内殿。

items.en: Microscopists used the room word for the box-like spaces they saw in cork.
items.cn: 显微观察者用这个「小室」词指他们在软木中看到的格子状空间。

items.en: Membrana meant a skin, a thin covering or parchment.
items.cn: 这个词意为皮、薄膜或羊皮纸。

items.en: The word for a limb is generally taken as the base of membrana, though the link is not certain.
items.cn: 表示「肢体」的词一般认为就是「膜」这个词的基底，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: English took the Latin noun for any thin sheet, anatomical or otherwise.
items.cn: 英语借入这个拉丁名词，指任何薄膜，解剖学内外皆可。

items.en: Microscopists named the boundary they could see at the edge of a cell; the molecular structure was worked out in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 显微观察者为他们在细胞边缘看到的界线命名；其分子结构在二十世纪才被阐明。

note.en: The first group shares the cell or membrane element; the second group names the same barrier technically or names neighbouring structures.
note.cn: 第一组共享「细胞」或「膜」的成分；第二组是同一屏障的技术名称，或相邻结构。

entries.definition: Any thin sheet covering or lining a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖或衬在某表面的任何薄膜。

entries.definition: Made of or like a membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指由膜构成的，或像膜一样的。

entries.definition: The basic unit of living tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指活组织的基本单位。

entries.definition: Relating to cells or divided into small compartments.
entries.definitionCN: 指与细胞有关的，或分成小格的。

entries.definition: The rigid outer layer of plant and bacterial cells.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物与细菌细胞外层的坚硬结构。

entries.definition: The technical synonym for the membrane around a cell.
entries.definitionCN: 指包住细胞的膜的技术同义词。

entries.definition: The double molecular sheet that makes up most of the membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成膜大部分的分子双层。

entries.definition: All the outer layers of a bacterium, membrane plus wall and capsule.
entries.definitionCN: 指细菌的全部外层，包括膜、壁与荚膜。

entries.definition: The lipid with a charged head that builds the bilayer.
entries.definitionCN: 指带电荷头部的脂质，构成双分子层。

entries.definition: A protein that detects a signal at the membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指在膜上探测信号的蛋白质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the room and its thin wall, then the doors and ears built into that wall.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「房间」与「薄墙」展开，再想到墙上开的门与耳朵。

normal.en: A cell is a room, so its membrane is the wall.
normal.cn: 细胞是一间屋子，细胞膜就是墙。

normal.en: The wall is two layers of lipid, heads out and tails in.
normal.cn: 这面墙由两层脂质构成，头朝外、尾朝内。

normal.en: Charged ions cannot cross alone, so proteins provide doors.
normal.cn: 带电离子不能独自穿过，蛋白质便提供门。

normal.en: The membrane is also the cell's ear, full of receptors.
normal.cn: 细胞膜也是细胞的耳朵，布满受体。

normal.en: Plant cells add a wall outside the membrane; bacteria wrap both in an envelope.
normal.cn: 植物细胞在膜外再加一层壁，细菌则把两者都裹进被膜里。

abstract.en: A boundary is not a prison; it is what makes an inside possible.
abstract.cn: 边界不是监狱，而是让「内部」得以存在的东西。

abstract.en: The thinner the wall, the more carefully it must choose what passes.
abstract.cn: 墙越薄，就越要仔细选择让什么通过。

abstract.en: Every cell listens at its skin before it acts.
abstract.cn: 每个细胞都先在皮肤上倾听，然后才行动。

examples.en: The cell membrane controls the movement of salts into the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 细胞膜控制盐分进入细胞质的运动。

examples.en: Freeze-fracture reveals proteins embedded in the cell membrane.
examples.cn: 冷冻断裂法显示出嵌在细胞膜中的蛋白质。

examples.en: Some viruses fuse with the cell membrane to enter.
examples.cn: 有些病毒与细胞膜融合而进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「塞尔·门布瑞恩」——一间小室（塞尔）外面绷着一层薄膜（门布瑞恩），就是细胞膜：细胞膜、质膜

root: 「细胞」出自拉丁语 cella「小室」，十七世纪被用于活组织单位；「膜」出自拉丁语 membrana「皮、羊皮纸」，一般认为来自 membrum「肢体」，但联系不确定；合成短语属十九世纪显微观察。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses build up from the boundary itself to its molecular sheet, its selectivity, its doors, its ears, its scaffolding, its variation across cells and its use as a model or target.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从边界本身逐步往上：分子薄片、选择性、门、耳朵、支架、在不同细胞中的差异，以及作为模型或靶点的用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glowing thin outline around a cell under a microscope, with dye stopping at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下一枚细胞被荧光勾出细边，染料在边沿停住。

branches.en: THE WALL AND ITS BUILD: the boundary, and the molecular double sheet that makes it.
branches.cn: 墙与做法：边界本身，以及构成它的分子双层。

branches.en: WHAT PASSES: selective permeability, and the proteins that open the doors.
branches.cn: 什么能过：选择性通透，以及开门的蛋白质。

branches.en: THE EAR: receptors that let a cell hear its surroundings.
branches.cn: 耳朵：让细胞听见周围环境的受体。

branches.en: THE SCAFFOLD: shape and anchoring for the cell's internal fibres.
branches.cn: 支架：为细胞内部纤维提供形状与锚定。

branches.en: THE VARIATIONS AND USES: membranes across cell types, and membranes as models or drug targets.
branches.cn: 差异与用途：不同细胞类型的膜，以及作为模型或药物靶点的膜。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin room plus a Latin skin, a plain description that later acquired a molecular meaning.
intro.cn: 这条短语是拉丁语的「房间」加「皮」，本是朴素描述，后来才获得分子层面的含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both nouns: the small room and the thin covering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供两个名词：小室与薄膜。

items.example: It is the source of cell and cellar.
items.exampleCN: 它是「细胞」与「地窖」等词的来源。

items.example: The biological sense dates from the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物学义可追溯到十七世纪。

items.example: It is the source of membrane.
It is generally taken as the base of the skin word, though not with certainty.
items.exampleCN: 它一般被认为是「膜」词的基底，但并不确定。

items.example: English uses it in anatomy and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 英语在解剖与化学中使用它。

items.example: It forms membranous, like a membrane.
It gives the technical synonym plasma membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它构成技术同义词「质膜」。

items.example: It names the molecules that build the bilayer.
It forms bilayer, the two-layer structure.
It forms semipermeable, letting some things through.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「半透的」，即只让部分物质通过。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「皮、膜」名词构成，义为「膜」
由「膜」加形容词词尾构成，义为「膜状的」
由拉丁「小室」名词构成，义为「细胞」
由「细胞」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞的」
由次级前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚细胞的」
由表示「在内」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「细胞内的」

definition_zh: adj. 野蛮的；残暴的；未开化的、粗鄙的；（古义）异族的、非希腊罗马的
definition_en: brutally cruel; uncivilised or crude in taste; in older use, of foreign peoples outside the Greek and Roman world
core_image: 卷宗里那种不该属于任何世纪的刑罚
scene: 法官读完卷宗，说这种刑罚不该出现在任何时代。 The judge closed the file and called the punishment barbaric, whatever the century.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：barbaric 指残暴野蛮；句意是法官合上卷宗，称这种刑罚无论放在哪个世纪都属于野蛮。

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Brutally cruel
senses.definition: shockingly cruel and without any restraint of civilised feeling
senses.definitionCN: 残酷得令人震惊，毫无文明情感的约束
senses.example: The court described the treatment as barbaric.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭称这种对待方式是残暴的。
senses.why: The word moved from naming difference to naming cruelty, so it now judges the act rather than the origin of the actor.
senses.whyCN: 该词由「指认差异」转为「指认残暴」，因此如今评判的是行为，而非行为者的出身。

senses.title: Uncivilised or crude
senses.definition: lacking refinement in manners, art, or taste
senses.definitionCN: 在举止、艺术或趣味上缺乏教养与打磨
senses.example: The hall was decorated with barbaric splendour.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅装饰得奢华而粗野。
senses.why: Here the judgement is about polish rather than pain: too much gold, too little restraint.
senses.whyCN: 这里的评判关乎「打磨」而非「痛苦」：金子太多，克制太少。

senses.title: Foreign, in old use
senses.definition: in older writing, belonging to peoples outside the Greek and Roman world
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文献中指希腊罗马世界之外的族群
senses.example: The chronicler wrote of barbaric tribes beyond the river.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史家写到河外的异族部落。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense: the word first imitated speech that sounded like bar bar to Greek ears.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语的原义：该词最初模仿在希腊人耳中听起来像「bar bar」的话语。

intro.en: Barbaric began as an imitation of unintelligible speech: bar bar. Greek turned that sound into a word for foreign, and history turned foreign into cruel.
intro.cn: barbaric 起初是对听不懂的话语的模仿：bar bar。希腊人把这个声音变成「异族」一词，历史又把「异族」变成了「残暴」。

items.en: Greek barbaros imitates speech that sounds like bar bar, so it first meant foreign.
items.cn: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿听起来像「bar bar」的话语，初义为「异族的」。

items.en: Greek barbarikos turns the noun into an adjective, of or like foreigners.
items.cn: 希腊语 barbarikos 把名词变为形容词，意为「异族的、像异族的」。

items.en: Latin barbaricus keeps the adjective for peoples outside the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语 barbaricus 保留该形容词，指帝国之外的族群。

items.en: English takes the word through French, still mainly meaning foreign and unpolished.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入该词，仍主要表示「异族的、未加雕琢的」。

items.en: Wars and travel writing push the word toward savage cruelty rather than mere difference.
items.cn: 战争与游记把词义推向残暴，而不再只是「不同」。

items.en: Modern use splits: barbaric marks cruelty, barbarous marks crude taste, barbarian names the person.
items.cn: 现代用法分化：barbaric 指残暴，barbarous 偏粗鄙，barbarian 指其人。

note.en: The look-alike group first separates the three barbar- relatives by what each one names, then adds two false friends; the near-meaning group grades cruelty from wild to unrefined.
note.cn: 形近组先把三个 barbar- 亲属按各自所指区分开，再加入两个假朋友；近义组把「残酷」由凶猛到粗鄙分级排列。

entries.definition: Rough and unrefined, also cruel.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鄙未开化的，也可指残暴。

entries.definition: A member of a people thought uncivilised.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为未开化族群的一员。

entries.definition: Someone who cuts hair and trims beards.
entries.definitionCN: 理发修面的人。

entries.definition: A drug that depresses the nervous system.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制神经系统的药物。

entries.definition: Violently wild and uncontrolled.
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛不驯的。

entries.definition: Showing no mercy or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无怜悯的。

entries.definition: Willing to cause suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于造成痛苦的。

entries.definition: Without the manners of an ordered society.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏有序社会礼教的。

normalIntro.en: Say bar bar aloud: that is what foreign speech sounded like to Greek ears, and barbaric is built on that stammer.
normalIntro.cn: 把 bar bar 念出声：这就是希腊人耳中异族语言的声音，而 barbaric 就建在这个「口吃」之上。

normal.en: Barbar- is the stammer, -ic is the adjective ending.
normal.cn: barbar- 是那个口吃声，-ic 是形容词词尾。

normal.en: Barbarian is the person; barbaric is the quality.
normal.cn: barbarian 指人，barbaric 指性质。

normal.en: Barbarity is the cruel act; barbarism is the crude state.
normal.cn: barbarity 指暴行，barbarism 指粗野状态。

normal.en: Barbaric has no -er form; use more barbaric.
normal.cn: barbaric 没有 -er 形式，比较级用 more barbaric。

normal.en: Barbaric splendour means rich but tasteless.
normal.cn: barbaric splendour 意为奢华却无品味。

abstract.en: A sound of not understanding, hardened into a verdict.
abstract.cn: 一声「听不懂」，硬化成了一句判词。

abstract.en: The moment difference is renamed as fault.
abstract.cn: 「不同」被改名为「过错」的那一刻。

abstract.en: Gold piled where restraint should stand.
abstract.cn: 本该站着克制的地方，堆满了金子。

examples.en: They condemned the barbaric treatment of prisoners.
examples.cn: 他们谴责对囚犯的残暴对待。

examples.en: The palace was a barbaric display of gold and mirrors.
examples.cn: 那座宫殿是金饰与镜子的粗野炫耀。

examples.en: More barbaric punishments were abolished that year.
examples.cn: 那一年废除了更野蛮的刑罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴巴里克」——听不清的「巴巴」声就是词根 barbar-，加 -ic 成形容词。记一条线：bar bar 听不懂 → 异族 → 未开化 → 残暴。人叫 barbarian，性质叫 barbaric。

root: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿异族语言「bar bar」之声，初义「非希腊的、异族的」；派生 barbarikos，经拉丁语 barbaricus、法语进入英语，约 1400 年作 barbaric。17 世纪战争与游记把词义推向残暴，现代与 barbarous「粗鄙」、barbarian「其人」分工。

sensesIntro.en: Read the three senses as a history: first foreign, then unpolished, finally cruel. The order of the senses is the order of the prejudice.
sensesIntro.cn: 把三个义项当成一段历史来读：先是异族，再是无教养，最后是残暴。义项的顺序就是偏见形成的顺序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a punishment in a closed file that belongs to no century
core.cn: 核心意象：合上的卷宗里那种不属于任何世纪的刑罚

branches.en: A sentence read out in a quiet court.
branches.cn: 安静法庭上宣读的判词。

branches.en: Gold leaf over every surface.
branches.cn: 每个表面都贴满金箔。

branches.en: Ornament with no empty space.
branches.cn: 不留一处空白的装饰。

branches.en: Tribes drawn beyond the river.
branches.cn: 地图上画在河外的部落。

branches.en: A verdict passed from outside.
branches.cn: 从外部下的一道判词。

intro.en: Barbaric is the reduplicated root barbar- plus -ic; the same root gives the person, the act and the state through different suffixes.
intro.cn: barbaric 是叠音词根 barbar- 加 -ic；同一词根通过不同后缀分别给出「人」「行为」与「状态」。

latinIntro.en: Latin barbarus and barbaricus carry the Greek word west; brutus, heavy and dull, supplies the near-synonym brutal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 barbarus 与 barbaricus 把希腊词西传；brutus「沉重迟钝」提供近义词 brutal。

definition_zh: 不能飞的（鸟）；无翅或翅退化的（昆虫）；家养后不再飞的禽类；演化中失去飞行能力的；比喻无法起步的
definition_en: lacking the ability to fly, whether because of anatomy, domestication, or evolutionary loss, and figuratively unable to get off the ground
core_image: 一只企鹅站在冰缘，鳍状的前肢垂在身侧，身后是它走不进去的天空
scene: 冰缘上，一群黑白相间的大鸟摇摇摆摆地朝繁殖群走去，它们的鳍肢只能划水，不能托起身体。 At the edge of the ice, the flightless birds shuffled inland toward their colony.
sceneCN: 这里 flightless 是「不能飞的」（第 1 个义项：身体结构上不具备飞行能力的鸟类）；句意为在冰缘，这些不能飞的鸟摇摇摆摆地朝内陆的繁殖群走去。

pos.zh: 不能飞的；无翅的；（昆虫）无飞行阶段的

derivatives.zh: 不能飞的状态；无飞行能力

senses.title: Birds That Cannot Fly
senses.definition: describing birds whose wings or flippers cannot lift them into the air
senses.definitionCN: 描述翅膀或鳍肢无法把身体托入空中的鸟类
senses.example: Penguins are flightless, but their flippers make them fast swimmers.
senses.exampleCN: 企鹅不能飞，但它们的鳍肢使它们成为游泳好手。
senses.why: flight names the capacity, and -less removes it; the word simply says the bird has no flight, without saying why.
senses.whyCN: flight 命名这种能力，-less 把它拿走；这个词只是说这种鸟没有飞行能力，并不解释原因。

senses.title: Insects Without Working Wings
senses.definition: used of insects that have no wings at all or only reduced, useless ones
senses.definitionCN: 用于完全没有翅膀、或只有退化无用翅膀的昆虫
senses.example: Many beetles living in caves are flightless and blind.
senses.exampleCN: 许多生活在洞穴里的甲虫既不能飞，也看不见。
senses.why: the suffix states an absence, so it applies to any insect that lacks the organ the noun presupposes.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀表示的是一种缺失，因此可用来指任何缺少名词所预设之器官的昆虫。

senses.title: Domesticated Breeds That No Longer Fly
senses.titleCN: 家养后不再飞的禽类品种
senses.definition: used of farm breeds whose bodies have grown too heavy or too stubby to fly
senses.definitionCN: 用于因身体过重或翅膀过短而无法飞行的家养品种
senses.example: The farm keeps a flightless duck breed for its eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场养一种不会飞的鸭品种，取用它的蛋。
senses.why: domestication removes the need and then the ability, so the adjective marks a loss produced by husbandry rather than by nature.
senses.whyCN: 驯化先取消需要，再取消能力，形容词因此标记的是饲养造成的丧失，而非自然造成的。

senses.title: Flight Lost in Evolution
senses.titleCN: 演化中失去飞行能力的（岛屿鸟类）
senses.definition: used of species whose ancestors flew but whose isolated populations lost that ability
senses.definitionCN: 用于祖先会飞、但孤立种群后来失去这种能力的物种
senses.example: Island rails became flightless within a few thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿上的秧鸡在几千年内就失去了飞行能力。
senses.why: on islands without predators, wings cost more than they earn, and the adjective records the outcome of that trade.
senses.whyCN: 在没有捕食者的岛上，翅膀的代价高于收益，这个形容词记录的正是这笔交易的结果。

senses.title: The Island Niche of Lost Flight
senses.titleCN: 岛屿生态中「不能飞」的生态位
senses.definition: the ecological role filled by species that give up flight on predator-free islands
senses.definitionCN: 在无捕食者岛屿上放弃飞行的物种所占据的生态角色
senses.example: Flightless grazers on remote islands often replace large herbivores.
senses.exampleCN: 偏远岛屿上不能飞的食草动物常替代大型植食者。
senses.why: the adjective becomes a niche label because the loss of flight reshapes how a species feeds and breeds.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词之所以成为生态位标签，是因为失去飞行会重塑一个物种取食与繁殖的方式。

senses.title: Figurative: Unable to Take Off
senses.titleCN: 比喻：无法起飞、被束缚的
senses.definition: figurative, describing a plan, career or person unable to get started or to move freely
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指计划、事业或人无法起步、无法自由行动
senses.example: The project was flightless from the start, short of funds and staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目从一开始就无法起飞，缺钱也缺人。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core image intact: wings may exist, but nothing lifts, and the ground holds.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻完整保留了核心意象：翅膀也许在，但没有东西能把它托起，地面牢牢拉住。

senses.title: The Wingless Stage of an Insect
senses.titleCN: 昆虫的无翅阶段（若虫、工蚁）
senses.definition: used of a stage in an insect's life, or a caste, that never develops wings
senses.definitionCN: 用于昆虫一生中某个从不长出翅膀的阶段或品级
senses.example: Worker ants are a flightless caste within a winged species.
senses.exampleCN: 工蚁是一个会飞的物种内部不能飞的品级。
senses.why: the species may fly, yet the stage does not, and the adjective marks the stage rather than the whole animal.
senses.whyCN: 物种会飞，这个阶段却不会；形容词标记的是阶段，而不是整个动物。

senses.title: Not Involving Flight at All
senses.titleCN: 字面：无需飞行的（设备、训练语境）
senses.definition: used of equipment, drills or training that involve no flying at all
senses.definitionCN: 用于完全不涉及飞行的设备、演练或训练
senses.example: Ground crews practise on a flightless simulator before touching a real aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 地勤人员在接触真机之前，先在不会飞的模拟器上练习。
senses.why: here the suffix negates the activity rather than a bird's anatomy, so the adjective simply means without any flying.
senses.whyCN: 这里的后缀否定的是活动本身，而不是鸟的身体构造，因此形容词只表示「不涉及任何飞行」。

intro.en: Flightless is an English compound: flight, from Old English flyht, plus -less, from Old English -lēas 'free from, lacking'. It names a body that lacks the flight the base word presupposes.
intro.cn: flightless 是一个英语复合词：flight（来自古英语 flyht）加 -less（古英语 -lēas「没有、免于」）。它命名的是一个缺少基词所预设之飞行能力的身体。

items.en: Flyht is the action noun from fleogan 'to fly' plus -t; it names both the act and the group that performs it.
items.cn: flyht 是由 fleogan「飞」加 -t 构成的动作名词，既指动作，也指做出该动作的群体。

items.en: Old English -lēas meant 'free from, without', and it already formed adjectives such as slǣplēas 'sleepless'.
items.cn: 古英语 -lēas 意为「没有、免于」，当时就已构成 slǣplēas「不眠的」一类形容词。

items.en: German -los and Dutch -loos are the same suffix, so the pattern is Germanic rather than borrowed from Latin.
items.cn: 德语 -los 与荷兰语 -loos 是同一后缀，可见这一构词模式属日耳曼语，而非从拉丁语借入。

items.en: The adjective appears in English only in the modern period, once natural history needed a plain word for birds that cannot fly.
items.cn: 这个形容词到近代英语才出现，是博物学需要一个朴素的说法来描述不会飞的鸟时造出来的。

items.en: The same construction yields harmless, sleepless, weightless and wingless, all built on a noun plus -less rather than on a Latin prefix.
items.cn: 同一构词法造出了 harmless、sleepless、weightless、wingless，全都建立在「名词 + -less」上，而不是拉丁前缀。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Germanic origin of -lēas is a reconstruction, and no firm first citation is available for the adjective flightless.
items.cn: 来源不确定：-lēas 在日耳曼语之前的来源属重构形式，形容词 flightless 也没有可靠的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds the base word and the -less formations that look like it; group two holds adjectives that describe the same incapacity from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是基词以及外形相似的 -less 构词；第二组是从别的角度描述同一种「不能飞」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun from which flightless is built; it names the capacity itself, while the -less form names its absence.
entries.definitionCN: flightless 所由构成的基词；它命名能力本身，而 -less 形式命名的是能力的缺失。

entries.definition: Flight plus -y 'given to', meaning fickle; the suffix adds a habit rather than removing a capacity, so the sense runs the other way.
entries.definitionCN: flight 加 -y「倾向于」，意为轻浮善变；后缀添加的是一种习性而非移除一种能力，词义方向正好相反。

entries.definition: Built on sight plus -less; it shares only the suffix, since sight comes from Old English gesiht and has nothing to do with flying.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sight 加 -less 构成；只共用后缀，sight 来自古英语 gesiht，与飞行毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built on weight plus -less; the shape is identical but the base belongs to the weighing family, not the flying one.
entries.definitionCN: 由 weight 加 -less 构成；外形完全相同，但基词属于「称重」词族，而非「飞行」词族。

entries.definition: Lacking wings outright; it names the missing organ, while flightless names the missing ability, which may survive in a wingless body.
entries.definitionCN: 指根本没有翅膀；它命名缺失的器官，而 flightless 命名缺失的能力，后者在没有翅膀的身体上也可能谈得上。

entries.definition: Kept from flying by an outside order or circumstance, as a grounded aircraft; the incapacity is temporary and imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 因外部命令或情况被禁止飞行，如停飞的飞机；这种不能飞是暂时的、外加的。

entries.definition: Confined to the ground by nature or circumstance; it is broader and more literary than flightless.
entries.definitionCN: 因天性或处境被限制在地面；比 flightless 更宽泛，也更有文学色彩。

entries.definition: A neutral technical negative used of species or stages that do not fly; it states the fact without implying loss.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的技术性否定词，用于不飞的物种或阶段；只陈述事实，不含「丧失」之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the base word, the real suffix and the real parallel formations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：基词、真实后缀与真实平行构词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: flight + -less: the suffix takes away exactly what the noun supplies.
normal.cn: flight + -less：后缀拿走的正是名词提供的那样东西。

normal.en: German -los and Dutch -loos prove the suffix is Germanic, not Latin.
normal.cn: 德语 -los 与荷兰语 -loos 证明这个后缀属日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

normal.en: harmless, sleepless, weightless, wingless: one pattern, many nouns.
normal.cn: harmless、sleepless、weightless、wingless：一个模式，多个名词。

normal.en: Penguins are the standard example: flippers for swimming, nothing for lifting.
normal.cn: 企鹅是标准例子：鳍肢用来游泳，没有东西用来升空。

normal.en: On islands the word becomes an ecological label, because loss of flight changes how a species lives.
normal.cn: 在岛屿上这个词变成生态学标签，因为失去飞行会改变一个物种的生活方式。

abstract.en: Picture a kite with a perfect frame and no wind beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只骨架完好、身下却没有风的风筝。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose top step ends at a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，最高一级尽头是一扇锁住的门。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of wings folded neatly and never opened again.
abstract.cn: 想象一对折得整整齐齐、再也不展开的翅膀。

examples.en: New Zealand once held dozens of flightless bird species.
examples.cn: 新西兰曾经有数十种不会飞的鸟类。

examples.en: The beetle's flightless females look almost like larvae.
examples.cn: 这种甲虫不能飞的雌性看起来几乎像幼虫。

examples.en: Without wind, the design remained flightless no matter how light it was.
examples.cn: 没有风，这个设计无论多轻都无法起飞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弗莱特莱斯」——翅膀像被剪掉一样轻，却怎么也升不起来 → 不能飞的。

root: flight（古英语 flyht，fleogan「飞」+ -t）+ -less（古英语 -lēas「缺乏、没有」，与德语 -los、荷兰语 -loos 同源）；-lēas 更早的来源属重构形式，形容词本身首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all deny one capacity. The denial can come from anatomy, from a wingless stage, from breeding, from evolution on islands, from the niche that loss creates, from a metaphor about plans, or from a context where no flying is involved at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在否定同一种能力。这种否定可能来自身体构造、无翅阶段、人工饲养、岛屿演化、丧失所造就的生态位、关于计划的比喻，或来自一个根本不涉及飞行的语境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wings present or absent, and the air never entered.
core.cn: 核心意象：翅膀也许在、也许不在，但那片天空始终没有被进入。

branches.en: ANATOMY: the bird or insect simply lacks the organ or the power.
branches.cn: 构造：鸟或昆虫干脆缺少器官或力量。

branches.en: LOSS BY CIRCUMSTANCE: breeding makes the body heavy, a caste or stage never grows wings.
branches.cn: 处境造成的丧失：饲养让身体变重，某个品级或阶段则从不长翅。

branches.en: EVOLUTION ON ISLANDS: flight is traded away and the loss becomes a way of life.
branches.cn: 岛屿演化：飞行被交换掉，丧失本身成了一种生活方式。

branches.en: METAPHOR: plans and people can also fail to lift off.
branches.cn: 比喻：计划和人同样可能升不起来。

branches.en: NO FLYING INVOLVED: the suffix can negate the activity, not the animal.
branches.cn: 不涉及飞行：后缀可以否定活动，而不是否定动物。

intro.en: Flightless is transparent: a Germanic noun for flying, plus a Germanic suffix of deprivation. The interest lies in how far that deprivation can be stretched.
intro.cn: flightless 的结构一目了然：一个表「飞」的日耳曼名词，加一个表「剥夺」的日耳曼后缀；值得玩味的是这种剥夺能被拉伸到多远。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies here: both halves are Germanic, and the nearest Latin idea, 'without', is expressed by a different prefix entirely.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有适用的拉丁词形：两半都属日耳曼语，而拉丁语中「没有」这一概念完全由另一个前缀表达。

items.structure: fleogan (Old English strong verb, class II)
items.meaning: to move through the air on wings
items.example: The base verb names the capacity that will be denied.
items.exampleCN: 基词动词命名的是后来被否定的那种能力。

items.meaning: the act of doing the verb
items.example: Flight is the act, not the actor.
items.exampleCN: flight 指动作，不指施动者。

items.example: The noun must exist before it can be denied.
items.exampleCN: 名词必须先存在，才谈得上被否定。

items.example: The suffix turns a possession into an absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「拥有」变成「没有」。

items.example: The adjective is a plain statement of absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是对缺失的朴素陈述。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to fly
items.example: Flightlessness evolved repeatedly on isolated islands.
items.exampleCN: 不能飞的状态在孤立岛屿上反复演化出来。

items.meaning: in a manner that involves no flying
items.example: The adverb is rare and mostly technical.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词罕用，多见于技术文字。

items.example: Wingless names the organ, flightless names the power.
items.exampleCN: wingless 指器官，flightless 指能力。

items.example: The same suffix produced slǣplēas in Old English.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀在古英语中造出了 slǣplēas。

items.meaning: the line along which a flying thing travels
items.example: A flightless bird has no flight path to record.
items.exampleCN: 不会飞的鸟没有飞行路线可记录。

definition_zh: 民族学；人种学；对民族的比较研究
definition_en: the comparative study of peoples and their cultures
core_image: 把许多民族的语言、亲缘与器物摆在一张长桌上比较
scene: 博物馆的展柜按语言与亲缘把各民族的器物并排摆开，这种排列背后是一门比较的学问。 Comparative ethnology groups peoples by language, kinship, and material culture.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnology 是「民族学」（第 1 个义项：对各民族进行比较研究的学科）；句意：比较民族学按语言、亲缘关系与物质文化给各民族归类。

derivatives.zh: ethnology 加 -ical 构成，指民族学的、以比较方法研究民族的
ethnology 加 -ist 构成，指研究民族学的学者
ethno-（民族）+ history，指结合文献与民族材料的民族史研究
ethno-（民族）+ linguistics，指研究语言与民族文化关系的学科

senses.title: The comparative study of peoples
senses.definition: the branch of learning that compares the cultures, languages, and social forms of different peoples
senses.definitionCN: 比较不同民族的文化、语言与社会形态的学科
senses.example: Ethnology asks why neighbouring peoples organise kinship so differently.
senses.exampleCN: 民族学追问：为什么相邻民族的亲属制度差别如此之大。
senses.why: Greek logos means reasoned account, so ethnology is not the writing of one people but reasoned comparison across many, which is why the word names a general science.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 logos 意为有理据的论说，所以 ethnology 不是写下某一个民族，而是对许多民族作有理据的比较，因此它命名的是一门总体性的学问。

senses.title: The study of origins and distribution
senses.definition: the older programme of classifying peoples by origin, migration, and physical or cultural traits
senses.definitionCN: 较早的研究纲领，按起源、迁徙以及体质或文化特征给民族分类
senses.example: Nineteenth-century ethnology often mixed classification with speculation.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的民族学常把分类与猜测混在一起。
senses.why: When the discipline was young, its main task was to place peoples on a map of descent and migration, and that historical programme still colours one sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科年轻时，主要任务是把各民族放到血统与迁徙的地图上，这个历史阶段的纲领至今仍构成该词的一个义项。

senses.title: Knowledge of one people or region
senses.titleCN: 对某一民族或地区的研究
senses.definition: the accumulated body of study devoted to a particular people or area
senses.definitionCN: 针对某个民族或某个地区积累起来的研究成果
senses.example: The museum holds a strong collection in the ethnology of the northern peoples.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆在北方各民族的民族学研究上收藏颇丰。
senses.why: Like other names ending in -ology, it can shift from the whole discipline to the total knowledge about one object, so a library can hold the ethnology of a single region.
senses.whyCN: 和其他以 -ology 结尾的学科名一样，它可以从整门学科转指关于某一对象的全部知识，所以一座图书馆可以收藏某一地区的民族学研究。

intro.en: Ethnology joins Greek ethnos, a people, with -logia, from logos, reasoned account or study.
intro.cn: ethnology 由希腊语 ethnos（民族）与 -logia（源自 logos，论说、研究）组合而成。

items.en: Ethnos means a people or a nation, a group sharing descent and custom.
items.cn: ethnos 指民族或族群，即共享血统与习俗的群体。

items.en: Logos means word, account, or reasoned discourse.
items.cn: logos 指言词、叙述或有理据的论说。

items.en: The ending -logia names a field of study or a body of accounts.
items.cn: 词尾 -logia 表示某一研究领域或一批论述。

items.en: Scholars of the eighteenth century coin ethnologia for the study of peoples.
items.cn: 十八世纪的学者造出 ethnologia 一词，指对民族的研究。

items.en: English adopts ethnology for the classification and comparison of peoples.
items.cn: 英语采用 ethnology，指对各民族的分类与比较。

items.en: As anthropology takes over fieldwork, ethnology narrows toward comparison and regional knowledge.
items.cn: 随着人类学接管田野工作，ethnology 的范围收窄，转向比较与区域知识。

note.en: Ethnology is the comparing half of the ethno- family, next to its own adjective and person noun, and to the neighbouring social sciences.
note.cn: ethnology 是 ethno- 词族中「比较研究」的那一半，与它自己的形容词、人物名词以及相邻的社会科学为伍。

entries.definition: relating to the comparative study of peoples
entries.definitionCN: 民族学的

entries.definition: a scholar who compares peoples and their cultures
entries.definitionCN: 民族学学者

entries.definition: the study of music in its social and cultural setting
entries.definitionCN: 民族音乐学

entries.definition: the wider study of human societies, cultures, and biology
entries.definitionCN: 人类学

entries.definition: the study of societies, institutions, and social behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 社会学

entries.definition: the traditional beliefs and stories of a people
entries.definitionCN: 民俗；民间传承

normalIntro.en: Ethnology is ethnos plus logos: a reasoned account laid out across many peoples at once.
normalIntro.cn: ethnology 是 ethnos 加 logos：把有理据的论说同时铺展在许多民族之上。

normal.en: Ethno- marks a people, as it does in ethnic and ethnography.
normal.cn: ethno- 标记「民族」，ethnic 与 ethnography 也是如此。

normal.en: The ending -logy means the study of, as in biology.
normal.cn: 词尾 -logy 表示「……学」，biology 也是这样。

normal.en: An ethnologist compares, while an ethnographer describes.
normal.cn: ethnologist 做比较，ethnographer 做描述。

normal.en: Ethnological museums arrange objects by people and by region.
normal.cn: 民族学博物馆按民族与地区陈列器物。

normal.en: Compare -graphy and -logy: writing one people, versus reasoning about many.
normal.cn: 对比 -graphy 与 -logy：一个是写下一个民族，一个是对许多民族作论说。

abstract.en: See a long table with the languages and kinship terms of many peoples laid out side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，上面并排摊着许多民族的语言与亲属称谓，对应第 1 个义项的「比较研究」。

abstract.en: See lines drawn on a map of migrations, arrows meeting and splitting over the centuries.
abstract.cn: 想象一张迁徙地图上画出的线条，箭头在数百年间汇聚又分叉，对应第 2 个义项的「起源与分布」。

abstract.en: See one shelf in a library given wholly to a single northern people.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆里整整一层书架只放关于某一个北方民族的研究，对应第 3 个义项的「区域知识」。

examples.en: Ethnology compares the kinship systems of neighbouring peoples.
examples.cn: 民族学比较相邻各民族的亲属制度。

examples.en: He teaches ethnology in a museum studies programme.
examples.cn: 他在一个博物馆研究项目中教授民族学。

examples.en: The library keeps a full run of the journal of ethnology.
examples.cn: 图书馆保存着这份民族学期刊的完整过刊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ethno 民族 + logy 学问」——研究各民族的学问；这只是拆词联想，与严格的词源考证并不等同。

root: 希腊语 ethnos（民族、族群）+ logos（论说、道理）→ -logia（某类研究）→ 新拉丁语 ethnologia → 英语 ethnology，核心义「对各民族作有理据的比较研究」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers the whole comparative discipline, then the older programme of origins and distribution, then the accumulated knowledge of one people or region.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指整门比较性的学科，再指较早的起源与分布研究纲领，最后指关于某一民族或地区积累起来的知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many peoples laid side by side on one long table for comparison.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多民族被并排摆在一张长桌上作比较。

branches.en: The comparative discipline is the central sense of the word.
branches.cn: 比较性的学科是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: Classifying peoples by origin is the historical programme inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 按起源给民族分类，是这门学科内部的历史纲领。

branches.en: Knowledge of one region is the discipline applied to a single object.
branches.cn: 关于某一地区的知识，是这门学科落到单一对象上的用法。

branches.en: Comparison and classification used to be two names for one task.
branches.cn: 比较与分类一度是同一件事的两个名字。

branches.en: Origins are argued from regional knowledge, and regional knowledge is organised by origin.
branches.cn: 起源问题靠区域知识来论证，区域知识又按起源来组织。

intro.en: Ethnology is a Greek compound: ethnos, a people, plus -logy from logos, reasoned account.
intro.cn: ethnology 是希腊语复合词：ethnos（民族）加 -logy（源自 logos，有理据的论说）。

latinIntro.en: New Latin ethnologia fixed the shape of the word before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁语 ethnologia 在英语借入之前就固定了这个词的词形。

items.example: Ethnos is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: ethnos 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Logos gives the reasoning half of the word.
items.exampleCN: logos 提供这个词「论说」的那一半。

items.meaning: a field of study or discourse
items.meaningCN: 表示某类研究或论述的后缀
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -logia 用来命名整门学科。

items.example: The prefix ethno- also builds ethnography.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ethno- 也构成 ethnography。

items.example: Ethnologia is the learned Latin form.
items.exampleCN: ethnologia 是学术拉丁语形式。

items.meaningCN: 由名词构成形容词的后缀

items.example: Ethnological collections are grouped by region.
items.exampleCN: 民族学藏品按地区分组。

items.meaningCN: 表示「从事某事的人」的后缀

definition_zh: 宇宙的；巨大的；至关重要的
definition_en: relating to the cosmos; huge in scale or significance
core_image: X 射线天文望远镜拍到的星系碰撞图，配着人类尺度下的一双手示意大小
scene: 纪录片里解说员说： The collision of two galaxies is a cosmic event that plays out over hundreds of millions of years.
sceneCN: 这里指「宇宙尺度上的」（第1个义项）；句意为两个星系的碰撞是一个在几亿年间展开的 cosmic 事件。

pos.zh: 宇宙的；巨大的；至关重要的

senses.title: Relating to the cosmos or outer space
senses.titleCN: 与宇宙或外太空有关的
senses.definition: the core scientific sense; anything that happens beyond Earth and its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 核心科学义项：地球和大气层以外发生的任何事
senses.example: Cosmic radiation constantly bombards the upper atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙辐射不断轰击高层大气。
senses.why: cosmic = of the cosmos, just like galactic = of a galaxy.
senses.whyCN: cosmic = 宇宙的，就像 galactic = 星系的。

senses.title: On an immense scale
senses.definition: informal usage: so large or so huge that it dwarfs normal human-scale numbers or events
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：大到超过人类日常尺度的数字或事件
senses.example: The budget gap was cosmic — billions of dollars over what anyone had projected.
senses.exampleCN: 预算缺口是 cosmic 的——比任何人预期的多几十亿美元。
senses.why: Like astronomical, cosmic can refer to things on the scale of the universe.
senses.whyCN: 和 astronomical 一样，cosmic 可以指宇宙尺度的东西。

senses.title: Cosmic dust, rays, background radiation
senses.titleCN: 宇宙尘、宇宙射线、宇宙背景辐射
senses.definition: scientific compounds: cosmic describes anything in space — dust, rays, noise, microwave background
senses.definitionCN: 科学复合词：cosmic 描述太空里的一切——尘、射线、噪声、微波背景
senses.example: Cosmic microwave background radiation is the echo of the Big Bang.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙微波背景辐射是大爆炸的回声。
senses.why: The adjective is widely attached to nouns in astronomy and astrophysics.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在天文和天体物理里广泛跟名词搭配。

senses.title: Cosmic importance or significance
senses.definition: used for events or decisions that seem as important as anything in the universe
senses.definitionCN: 用于重要得像宇宙里最关键的事件或决定
senses.example: To a child, losing a favourite toy can feel of cosmic importance.
senses.exampleCN: 对小孩来说，丢了最喜欢的玩具可能觉得是 cosmic 级别的事。
senses.why: Hyperbole borrows the largest scale to mean the most important.
senses.whyCN: 夸张借最大的尺度来指最重要的。

senses.title: Cosmic justice or cosmic order
senses.definition: used to describe a moral or natural order that is larger than human society
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述比人类社会更大的道德或自然秩序
senses.example: Some people believe in cosmic justice that balances the wrongs of this life.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人相信 cosmic 正义会平衡这一世的冤屈。
senses.why: Cosmic carries the 'ordered whole' sense from its Greek root kosmos.
senses.whyCN: Cosmic 带着希腊语词根 kosmos 的「有序整体」含义。

senses.title: Cosmic vs astronomical vs galactic
senses.definition: cosmic = whole universe; astronomical = of astronomy or huge; galactic = of galaxies; the scales grow smaller
senses.definitionCN: cosmic = 整个宇宙；astronomical = 天文学的或巨大的；galactic = 星系的；尺度逐个变小
senses.example: Cosmic events span billions of galaxies; galactic events span one galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: Cosmic 事件跨越几十亿星系；galactic 事件只跨一个星系。
senses.why: The progression maps nicely: cosmic > astronomical > galactic.
senses.whyCN: 这个阶梯很清楚：cosmic > astronomical > galactic。

senses.title: Cosmic in popular culture and New Age
senses.titleCN: 流行文化和新世纪运动里的 cosmic
senses.definition: used for anything feeling mystical, universal or out of the ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 用来指神秘的、普遍的或不普通的事物
senses.example: The festival had a cosmic vibe — everyone felt connected to something bigger.
senses.exampleCN: 那个节日有一种 cosmic 的氛围——人人觉得和更伟大的东西连上了。
senses.why: New Age culture picked up cosmic because it evokes vastness, mystery and unity.
senses.whyCN: 新世纪运动喜欢 cosmic 因为它唤起浩瀚、神秘、合一。

senses.title: Cosmic rays and particle physics
senses.definition: high-energy particles from space that hit Earth's atmosphere; studied by particle physicists
senses.definitionCN: 来自太空、轰击地球大气的高能粒子；由粒子物理学家研究
senses.example: Cosmic rays discovered new fundamental particles before accelerators could.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线在加速器之前就发现了新的基本粒子。
senses.why: Cosmic rays are nature's own particle accelerator — cheaper and more powerful than anything we can build.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙射线是大自然自己的粒子加速器——比我们能造的都便宜且强大。

intro.en: cosmic is the adjective of cosmos: Greek kosmos (ordered universe) + -ic adjective suffix.
intro.cn: cosmic 是 cosmos 的形容词：希腊语 kosmos（有秩序的宇宙）+ -ic 形容词后缀。

items.en: kosmos 'order, ornament, universe' → cosmic via Latin and French.
items.cn: kosmos「秩序、装饰、宇宙」→ 经拉丁语和法语 → cosmic。

items.en: cosmic appeared in English in the early 17th century, borrowed from Latin cosmicus.
items.cn: cosmic 17 世纪早期进入英语，借自拉丁语 cosmicus。

items.en: With the growth of astrophysics in the 20th century, cosmic became attached to dozens of scientific compounds.
items.cn: 20 世纪天体物理成长时，cosmic 与几十个科学复合词搭在一起。

items.en: The 'huge scale' sense developed alongside astronomical and galactic in the 20th century.
items.cn: 「巨大尺度」的义项在 20 世纪和 astronomical, galactic 一起发展起来。

items.en: New Age writers and musicians adopted cosmic in the 1960s and 1970s.
items.cn: 1960-70 年代新世纪作家和音乐人采用 cosmic。

items.en: Scientific, figurative and New Age senses all remain active.
items.cn: 科学、比喻、新世纪的义项今天都活跃。

note.en: Group one shares the cosm- root; group two compares cosmic to other scale adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cosm- 词根；第二组把 cosmic 和其他尺度形容词对比。

entries.definition: The noun that cosmic describes.
entries.definitionCN: cosmic 描述的那个名词。

entries.definition: Study of the cosmos; cosmic events are often studied here.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙学；cosmic 事件常在其中研究。

entries.definition: One who studies cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙学家。

entries.definition: Study of how the cosmos began.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙起源论。

entries.definition: Huge in scale; of astronomy. Overlaps strongly with cosmic.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大尺度的；天文学的。与 cosmic 强烈重叠。

entries.definition: Of galaxies; smaller than cosmic, bigger than stellar.
entries.definitionCN: 星系的；比 cosmic 小，比 stellar 大。

entries.definition: Of stars themselves; smaller than galactic or cosmic.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星本身的；比 galactic 或 cosmic 小。

entries.definition: Applying everywhere; different angle from cosmic's 'scale' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 到处适用的；与 cosmic 的「尺度」义角度不同。

normalIntro.en: cosmic = of the cosmos.
normalIntro.cn: cosmic = 宇宙的。

normal.en: cosmos + -ic = cosmic, just like physics + -ic = physic (archaic for physical).
normal.cn: cosmos 加 -ic 构成 cosmic。

normal.en: Cosmic rays come from outer space.
normal.cn: 宇宙射线来自太空。

normal.en: The cosmic microwave background is the echo of the Big Bang.
normal.cn: 宇宙微波背景是大爆炸的回声。

normal.en: A cosmic event is so big it dwarfs everything else.
normal.cn: 一个 cosmic 事件大到其他一切都渺小。

normal.en: Cosmic justice balances the wrongs of the whole universe.
normal.cn: 宇宙正义平衡整个宇宙的冤屈。

abstract.en: The quiet hum of radiation left over from the beginning.
abstract.cn: 开端留下的辐射的安静嗡嗡声。

abstract.en: Something vast, ancient, and indifferent — that still gives us our atoms.
abstract.cn: 浩瀚、古老、冷漠的存在——但给了我们身上的每一个原子。

abstract.en: A word that can describe a supernova or a song, a budget gap or a love affair.
abstract.cn: 一个可以描述超新星或一首歌、预算缺口或一段爱情的词。

examples.en: Cosmic dust is one of the key ingredients for forming new stars and planets.
examples.cn: 宇宙尘是形成新恒星和行星的关键成分之一。

examples.en: To a four-year-old, finding their lost teddy bear feels of cosmic importance.
examples.cn: 对四岁小孩来说，找到丢失的泰迪熊感觉是 cosmic 级别的事。

examples.en: The team detected a burst of cosmic rays that could not be explained by known sources.
examples.cn: 团队探测到一次无法用已知来源解释的宇宙射线爆发。

dict_mnemonic.text: cosmos（宇宙）+ -ic（...的）= 宇宙的

root: kosmos（希腊语，秩序、宇宙）→ cosmic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the strict scientific adjective, through scale, compounds, importance, justice, terminology, New Age and particle physics.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从严格科学形容词出发，经过尺度、复合词、重要性、正义、术语、新世纪、粒子物理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: Earth as a blue dot against the black cosmos, speckled with galaxies.
core.cn: 核心意象：地球是宇宙黑底上的一个蓝点，点缀着星系。

intro.cn: cosmic = cosmos + -ic；-ic 是英语里借自希腊语的常见形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek -ikos → Latin -icus → English -ic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 -ikos → 拉丁 -icus → 英语 -ic。

definition_zh: 不合理的；不理智的；过分的；不公道的
definition_en: not fair or sensible, or going beyond what is acceptable
core_image: 有人非要在深夜里把音量调到最大
scene: 邻居把音箱搬到阳台上，说晚上开派对是理所当然的事。 It seems unreasonable to play music so loudly at that hour.
sceneCN: 这里 unreasonable 是「不合理的」（第 1 个义项：讲不通、没道理）；句意为那个钟点把音乐放得那么响实在说不过去。深夜把音量调到最大的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不合理地；过度地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不合理；不通情理」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「合理的；讲道理的」
同源名词，义为「理由；理性」
同源名词，义为「推理；论证」

senses.title: Not guided by good sense
senses.definition: not based on good judgement, so that others cannot follow it
senses.definitionCN: 不建立在良好判断之上，别人无法理解
senses.example: It is unreasonable to expect an answer within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一小时内得到答复是不合情理的。
senses.why: The word is the negative of reasonable, whose base is reason, the power of working things out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 reasonable 的反面，而词根 reason 指的正是推想、讲道理的能力。

senses.title: Asking for more than is fair
senses.definition: used of demands or prices that go beyond what is fair
senses.definitionCN: 形容提出过分要求或开出过高价格
senses.example: The hotel charges an unreasonable price for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆的早餐要价过高。
senses.why: Once a demand stops following reason, it also stops respecting the fair line, and the excess sense follows.
senses.whyCN: 要求一旦不再讲道理，也就不再顾惜那条公平线，于是「过分」这层意思随之而来。

senses.title: A person who will not listen to sense
senses.definition: used of a person who refuses to be persuaded by argument
senses.definitionCN: 形容听不进道理、怎么劝都没用的人
senses.example: He became unreasonable when anyone mentioned the money.
senses.exampleCN: 谁一提到那笔钱，他就变得不讲道理。
senses.why: When a person cuts himself off from reason, the absence of reason becomes a trait of character.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人把自己和道理隔开，那份「没有道理」就变成了一种性格。

senses.title: Not fair to someone
senses.definition: used of treatment or rules that are unfair to a person
senses.definitionCN: 形容对某人不公平的对待或规矩
senses.example: The rules seem unreasonable to anyone working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何上夜班的人来说，这些规矩都不公道。
senses.why: A rule that no sound reason supports is felt by the people under it as plain injustice.
senses.whyCN: 一条得不到正当理由支撑的规矩，落到受它管的人身上就是明显的不公。

senses.title: Not justified by logic
senses.definition: used of an argument or belief that does not follow from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容论证或信念与证据对不上
senses.example: The conclusion is unreasonable because the evidence does not support it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结论说不通，因为证据并不支持它。
senses.why: In argument the word narrows to its literal core: the steps of reasoning are missing.
senses.whyCN: 在论证中，这个词收窄到最字面的核心：推理的步骤缺失了。

intro.en: A negative prefix over an adjective built on reason, itself from Latin ratio through French.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在由 reason 构成的形容词上，而 reason 经法语来自拉丁语 ratio。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and negates adjectives freely.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，可自由加在形容词前表示否定。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning, account, and the faculty of reasoning.
items.cn: ratio 意为「计算、说明」，也指推理的能力。

items.en: Raison carried the same senses of account and judgement into French.
items.cn: raison 把「说明」与「判断」的意思带进法语。

items.en: Reason enters English meaning both a cause given and the mind that gives it.
items.cn: reason 进入英语时兼指「给出的理由」与「给出理由的心智」。

items.en: Reasonable and then unreasonable are formed, and the negative spreads to prices, demands, and people.
items.cn: 先有 reasonable，后有 unreasonable，否定义继而扩展到价格、要求与人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the reason family, and the near-meaning group collects words of excess and unfairness.
note.cn: 形近组沿 reason 词族展开，近义组汇集表示过分与不公的词。

entries.definition: sensible and fair
entries.definitionCN: 合理的；公道的

entries.definition: in an unfair or excessive way
entries.definitionCN: 不合理地；过度地

entries.definition: a cause or the power to judge
entries.definitionCN: 理由；理性

entries.definition: the process of thinking things through
entries.definitionCN: 推理；论证

entries.definition: so silly that it cannot be believed
entries.definitionCN: 荒谬的

entries.definition: far more than is proper
entries.definitionCN: 过度的

entries.definition: not just or equal
entries.definitionCN: 不公平的

entries.definition: showing good judgement
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；通情达理的

normalIntro.en: The word is the negative of an adjective everyone learns early, so its parts are plain.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是人人早就会的形容词的否定形式，部件一目了然。

normal.en: Un- plus reasonable: not open to reason at all.
normal.cn: un- 加 reasonable：完全没法讲道理。

normal.en: An unreasonable demand and an unreasonable price are the two fixed collocations.
normal.cn: an unreasonable demand 与 an unreasonable price 是两个固定搭配。

normal.en: The adverb unreasonably often modifies refuse and complain.
normal.cn: 副词 unreasonably 常修饰 refuse 与 complain。

normal.en: Reason, reasonable, and reasoning share the Latin root ratio.
normal.cn: reason、reasonable、reasoning 共享拉丁词根 ratio。

normal.en: Legal English uses unreasonable of terms that no fair person would accept.
normal.cn: 法律英语里 unreasonable 指任何通情达理的人都不会接受的条件。

abstract.en: Hear loud music from a balcony long after midnight.
abstract.cn: 在过了午夜很久之后听见阳台上传来很响的音乐。

abstract.en: See a customer shout at a clerk over a coin.
abstract.cn: 看见有人为一枚硬币对店员大喊。

abstract.en: Feel your hand stop moving on a clock that will not agree.
abstract.cn: 感受你的手停在一只怎么也对不上的钟上。

examples.en: It is unreasonable to blame the driver for a delay he cannot control.
examples.cn: 把司机控制不了的延误怪在他头上是不合情理的。

examples.en: The shop was criticised for charging unreasonable prices during the festival.
examples.cn: 这家店因节日期间要价过高而受到批评。

examples.en: She refused to argue with a friend who had become unreasonable.
examples.cn: 她拒绝再跟一个已经听不进道理的朋友争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不理事儿」——别人摆事实讲道理，俺不理那套，这种做法自然就显得不合理。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ reasonable（合理的），reasonable 由 reason 加 -able 构成，reason 源自拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）经古法语 raison 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One root idea, showing no trace of reason, branches into outrage, resistance, unfair treatment, and weak proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个根义「看不到道理」，分出过火、倔强、不公与推理站不住四路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning the volume knob to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把音量旋钮拧到最顶。

branches.en: The logic branch: a request no sound mind could follow.
branches.cn: 事理分支：清醒的人都跟不上的要求。

branches.en: The excess branch: prices and demands past the fair line.
branches.cn: 过度分支：越过公平线的价格与要求。

branches.en: The person branch: a friend who stops listening.
branches.cn: 人物分支：一个不再听劝的朋友。

branches.en: The fairness branch: treatment that singles someone out.
branches.cn: 公平分支：只针对某人的对待。

branches.en: The argument branch: a conclusion that does not follow.
branches.cn: 论证分支：推不出来的结论。

intro.en: A native negative prefix and a word-forming suffix sit on the ordinary noun for reason.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀与构词后缀都压在日常名词 reason 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is ratio, reckoning, with the verb reri behind it, to think or suppose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 ratio（计算），其后的动词 reri 意为「思考、推想」。

items.example: He gave no reason for leaving.
items.exampleCN: 他没有给出离开的理由。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He objected unreasonably to every plan.
items.exampleCN: 他对每个计划都不讲道理地反对。
她给出了有理有据的回答。

definition_zh: 装备；配备；使有能力
definition_en: to supply someone or something with the tools or skills needed
core_image: 出发前把工具一件件装进背包
scene: 学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。 The school equipped every lab with new microscopes.
sceneCN: 这里 equipped 是 equip 的过去式，表示「配备」（第 1 个义项：提供所需的工具或设备）；句意：学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。

senses.title: To supply with tools or gear
senses.definition: to provide a person or place with the tools, machines, or gear needed
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需的工具、机器或装备
senses.example: The team was equipped with maps and radios.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍配备了地图和无线电。
senses.why: The word came from fitting out a ship, so the basic sense is supplying the necessary gear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指为船只配备物资，因此基本含义是提供必需的装备。

senses.title: To prepare someone with skills
senses.definition: to give someone the knowledge or skills needed for a task
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人完成任务所需的知识或技能
senses.example: The course equips students to work in hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程使学生有能力在医院工作。
senses.why: Equipment can be mental as well as physical, so the verb extends to training.
senses.whyCN: 装备既可以是物质的，也可以是头脑中的，所以动词扩展到培训。

senses.title: To fit out a place
senses.definition: to furnish a room, building, or vehicle with what it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为房间、建筑或车辆配置所需设备
senses.example: They equipped the new kitchen with modern appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为新厨房配置了现代电器。
senses.why: The same supplying action applies to places and vehicles, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 同样的供给动作也适用于场所和车辆，而不只是人。

intro.en: Equip comes from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic word for ship.
intro.cn: equip 来自古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资），可能源于日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 一词意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备物资。

items.en: The word extends to fitting out a person or army.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到为个人或军队配备。

items.en: Equip enters English with the gear sense.
items.cn: equip 以「装备」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of preparing with skills.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「以技能作准备」的含义。

note.en: Equip is a supplying verb, closely tied to equipment and to words for furnishing.
note.cn: equip 是表示供给的动词，与 equipment 以及表示配置的词关系紧密。

entries.definition: the tools and gear needed
entries.definitionCN: 设备；装备

entries.definition: having the needed gear
entries.definitionCN: 装备好的

entries.definition: the act of supplying gear
entries.definitionCN: 装备的过程

entries.definition: to supply a room with furniture
entries.definitionCN: 为房间配置家具

entries.definition: to provide what is needed
entries.definitionCN: 供应；提供

entries.definition: to supply with weapons
entries.definitionCN: 武装；配备武器

normalIntro.en: Equip began as fitting out a ship; now you can equip a lab, a team, or a student.
normalIntro.cn: equip 最初指为船只配备物资；现在可以为实验室、队伍或学生配备所需。

normal.en: Equip with means supply with.
normal.cn: equip with 表示配备。

normal.en: A fully equipped kitchen has every tool you need.
normal.cn: fully equipped 的厨房拥有你需要的每样工具。

normal.en: The noun equipment is uncountable.
normal.cn: 名词 equipment 是不可数名词。

normal.en: A course can equip you for a career.
normal.cn: 一门课程可以让你有能力从事某种职业。

normal.en: Compare supply: supply is broader, equip stresses gear or preparation.
normal.cn: 对比 supply：supply 更宽泛，equip 强调装备或准备。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor loading ropes and lanterns onto a ship.
abstract.cn: 想象水手把绳索和灯笼装上船。

abstract.en: Imagine a hiker checking each item in a backpack.
abstract.cn: 想象徒步者逐一检查背包里的物品。

abstract.en: Think of a student leaving a class with a new skill.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生带着新技能走出课堂。

examples.en: Rescue teams were equipped with warm clothing.
examples.cn: 救援队配备了保暖衣物。

examples.en: The training equips nurses to handle emergencies.
examples.cn: 这项培训使护士有能力处理紧急情况。

examples.en: They equipped the office with new computers.
examples.cn: 他们为办公室配备了新电脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + quip」——出发前把工具「配齐」，就是装备；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资）→ 中古英语 equip，核心义「把所需之物配齐」，引申为使有能力。

sensesIntro.en: Equip starts with supplying gear, extends to preparing people with skills, and applies to fitting out places.
sensesIntro.cn: equip 从提供装备开始，扩展到以技能培养人，并适用于为场所配置设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a backpack filled with every tool the trip needs.
core.cn: 核心意象：背包里装满旅途所需的每样工具。

branches.en: Supplying tools is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 提供工具是基本的物质义项。

branches.en: Supplying skills extends gear to the mind.
branches.cn: 提供技能把装备扩展到头脑。

branches.en: Fitting out a place applies the same action to rooms.
branches.cn: 为场所配置设备把同一动作用于房间。

branches.en: A lab and a hiker are both fitted out with gear.
branches.cn: 实验室与徒步者都被配齐了装备。

branches.en: Both tools and training prepare someone for a task.
branches.cn: 工具与培训都让人为任务做好准备。

intro.en: Equip is a French fitting-out verb, with English equipment and equipped built from it.
intro.cn: equip 是法语中表示「配备」的动词，英语由它构成 equipment 与 equipped。

latinIntro.en: The French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably comes from a Germanic word for ship.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 esquiper（为船只配备）可能来自日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.example: Skip is the probable ship root.
items.exampleCN: skip 是可能表示「船」的词根。

items.example: Esquiper starts as a sailing word.

items.meaning: forming a past form or adjective

items.exampleCN: equipped 描述准备好的状态。
equipping 指正在进行的动作。
fully 常与 equipped 搭配。

definition_zh: 内在本质的；本身价值的；内在动机的；内禀的；内部的（肌肉）；内蕴的（曲率）；本征的（半导体）；内生的（增长）
definition_en: belonging to the inner nature of a thing and measured without reference to anything outside it
core_image: 拍卖台上摆着一幅无人出价的旧素描，鉴定师却只说它的价值不在标签上
scene: 拍卖行把一幅无人问津的旧素描摆上台面，鉴定师却说它的分量不在价签上。 The old sketch has an intrinsic worth that no auction price can measure.
sceneCN: 这里指事物自身所具有、不由外界定价的价值（第 2 个义项：不依赖外部评价的内在价值）；句意为这幅旧素描有一种拍卖价量不出的内在价值。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「本质上；就其自身而言」
由该形容词的词干加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「内在性；固有性」，多用于哲学
由对应的拉丁「在外」形式进入英语，义为「外在的；外来的」，是与目标词成对的反义对照词

senses.title: Belonging to a thing's own nature
senses.definition: forming part of what something is in itself, independent of how others regard it
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物自身之所是，与别人如何看待它无关
senses.example: Curiosity seems intrinsic to the human mind.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心似乎是人心本身固有的。
senses.why: The Latin word meant 'on the inside', so a quality located within a thing's own nature is intrinsic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「在内侧」，因此位于事物自身本性之中的性质就是内在的。

senses.title: Worth that is not set by a market
senses.definition: value that a thing has in itself, apart from price, usefulness or what buyers will pay
senses.definitionCN: 事物自身即有的价值，与价格、用途或买家的出价无关
senses.example: Philosophers debate whether art has intrinsic value.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论艺术是否具有内在价值。
senses.why: If worth is inside the thing, then an outside price can measure it only indirectly, if at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果价值在事物内部，那么外部价格至多只能间接地量到它。

senses.title: Drive that comes from within
senses.definition: motivation arising from interest or enjoyment rather than from external reward or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 由兴趣或乐趣产生的动机，而非来自外部奖励或压力
senses.example: Intrinsic motivation keeps volunteers coming back.
senses.exampleCN: 内在动机让志愿者一再回来。
senses.why: The source of the drive sits inside the person, which is exactly what the word locates inside.
senses.whyCN: 动力的源头在人的内部，而这正是这个词所定位的「内侧」。

senses.title: A property independent of amount
senses.titleCN: 与数量多少无关的性质
senses.definition: in physics, a property of a material that does not change when the sample size changes
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中不随样品大小改变的材料性质
senses.example: Density is intrinsic; mass is not.
senses.exampleCN: 密度是内禀性质，质量不是。
senses.why: A property that stays the same whether you take a gram or a tonne belongs to the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 无论取一克还是一吨都不变的性质，属于物质自身。

senses.title: Muscles lying inside an organ
senses.definition: in anatomy, said of muscles whose origin and insertion lie within the structure they move
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中起止点都位于其所运动结构内部的肌肉
senses.example: The intrinsic muscles of the hand control the fingers finely.
senses.exampleCN: 手部内在肌精细地控制手指。
senses.why: Anatomy contrasts muscles inside an organ with ones that enter it from outside.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把器官内部的肌肉与从外部伸入的肌肉相对照。

senses.title: Curvature measurable from inside
senses.definition: in geometry, a curvature determined by measurements within the surface itself, without embedding it in a larger space
senses.definitionCN: 几何中只靠曲面内部的测量即可确定的曲率，无需把曲面嵌入更大空间
senses.example: Intrinsic curvature can be detected by triangles on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 内蕴曲率可以通过曲面上的三角形测出。
senses.why: If the measurement needs nothing outside, the property is literally intrinsic to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 若测量不需要任何外部条件，该性质就字面地内在于曲面之中。

senses.title: Pure, undoped material
senses.definition: in electronics, said of a semiconductor whose behaviour comes from its own pure crystal, with no added impurities
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中行为来自纯净晶体本身、未添加杂质的半导体
senses.example: Intrinsic silicon conducts far less than doped silicon.
senses.exampleCN: 本征硅的导电性远低于掺杂硅。
senses.why: Its electrical behaviour is a property of the pure material, not of anything added from outside.
senses.whyCN: 它的电学行为来自纯净材料本身，而不是外部添加物。

senses.title: Growth generated from inside
senses.definition: in economics, growth produced by internal factors such as knowledge and investment in people, not by outside shocks
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中由知识、对人的投资等内部因素产生的增长，而非外部冲击带来
senses.example: Intrinsic growth models stress education over foreign aid.
senses.exampleCN: 内生增长模型强调教育胜过外国援助。
senses.why: The model looks for the causes of growth inside the economy rather than outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这类模型在经济体内部寻找增长原因，而不是在外部寻找。

intro.en: Intrinsic comes from Late Latin intrinsecus 'inwardly, on the inside', built on intra 'within' and secus 'alongside'. French intrinsèque carried it into English in the seventeenth century, paired with extrinsic. The direct source is clear; the earlier makeup of secus is still debated.
intro.cn: intrinsic 来自晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「向内的、在内侧的」，由 intra「在内」与 secus「沿着、旁边」构成。法语 intrinsèque 在十七世纪把它带进英语，并与 extrinsic 成对。直接来源清楚；更早的 secus 构成仍有争议。

items.en: Intra meant within or inside, and it still appears in English words such as intravenous.
items.cn: intra 意为在……之内，至今出现在 intravenous 等英语词中。

items.en: Secus meant alongside or beside; its further origin is disputed, so the internal makeup of the compound is not certain.
items.cn: secus 意为沿着、在旁边；它更早的来源有争议，因此这个复合词的内部构成并非确证。

items.en: The adverb meant inward or on the inside, and it described what belongs to a thing from within.
items.cn: 这个副词意为向内、在内侧，描述从内部属于某物的东西。

items.en: Its partner meant from outside, and the pair intrinsic and extrinsic still divide inner nature from external circumstance.
items.cn: 与之配对的形式意为「从外部」，如今「内在」与「外在」这一对仍用于区分本性与外部环境。

items.en: English took intrinsic through French for qualities belonging to a thing itself, especially in philosophy and theology.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个词，用于属于事物自身的性质，尤其在哲学与神学中。

items.en: Physics, anatomy, geometry and economics each gave the word a measured meaning where 'inside' can be tested.
items.cn: 物理学、解剖学、几何学与经济学各自给这个词一个可检验的「内部」含义。

note.en: The first group is the same word family with its opposite; the second group holds near synonyms that locate qualities differently.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族及其对立词；第二组是同样描述性质归属、但定位方式不同的近义词。

entries.definition: By its own nature, without reference to outside standards; it marks the source of value.
entries.definitionCN: 就其自身本性而言，不参照外部标准；标出价值的来源。

entries.definition: The quality of belonging to a thing's inner nature; a rare philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物内在本性的性质；少见的哲学名词。

entries.definition: Coming from outside, such as reward, price or circumstance; the exact opposite partner.
entries.definitionCN: 来自外部的东西，如奖励、价格或环境；正是与之相对的另一半。

entries.definition: An older variant spelling of the same adjective, now mostly replaced by the shorter form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较早异体拼法，如今多被较短的形取代。

entries.definition: Stuck to a subject so that it cannot be removed; it stresses attachment, while the target word stresses inner nature.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于主体而无法去除；强调「附着」，而目标词强调「内在本质」。

entries.definition: Present from birth; it marks a starting point in time rather than a location inside a nature.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有；标出时间上的起点，而非本性内部的位置。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be itself; stronger than a mere inner quality.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为自身；比单纯「内在性质」更强。

entries.definition: Designed into a product; the everyday word for what is installed rather than grown from within.
entries.definitionCN: 设计进产品里的；是日常说法，指装进去而非从内部长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'within': intrinsic value is the value inside the thing, not on the price tag.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在内」：内在价值是事物里面的价值，不在价签上。

normal.en: The family runs intrinsically, intrinsicality and the paired opposite extrinsic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本质上、内在性，以及与它成对的外在的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark value and drive: intrinsic value, intrinsic motivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出价值与动力：内在价值、内在动机。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: intrinsic property, intrinsic semiconductor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：内禀性质、本征半导体。

normal.en: Its opposite is extrinsic, which puts the source outside the thing.
normal.cn: 它的对立词是 extrinsic，把来源放在事物外部。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose shine comes from its own metal, not the light in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的光泽来自它自己的金属，而不是房间里的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who trains because the running itself feels good.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者训练，因为跑这件事本身让他舒服。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose warmth comes from its stones, not from a heater.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子的暖意来自石头本身，而不是暖气。

examples.en: The painting's intrinsic value lies in its brushwork, not its price.
examples.cn: 这幅画的内在价值在笔法，而不在价格。

examples.en: Children learn faster when motivation is intrinsic.
examples.cn: 当动机来自内心时，孩子学得更快。

examples.en: Conductivity is an intrinsic property of the pure crystal.
examples.cn: 导电性是纯晶体的内禀性质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印吹壳」——印在壳子最里面那一层，从外看不见，就是内在的

root: 拉丁 intra「在内」+ secus「沿着、旁边」→ 晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「内侧的」→ 法语 intrinsèque → 英语 intrinsic；与 extrinsecus「外在的」成对。secus 的更早来源尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place a quality inside its owner: in a nature, a value, a motive, a material property, an organ, a surface, a crystal or an economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某种性质放在所有者内部：放在本性里、价值里、动机里、材料性质里、器官里、曲面里、晶体里，或经济体里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality that lives inside a thing, so outside measures can only approach it.
core.cn: 核心意象：住在事物内部的一种性质，外部量度只能靠近它。

branches.en: THE NATURE SENSE: what a thing is in itself, apart from outside opinion.
branches.cn: 本性义：某物自身之所是，与外部看法无关。

branches.en: THE VALUED AND MOTIVATED SIDE: worth not set by a market, and interest that needs no reward.
branches.cn: 价值与动力一面：不由市场定价的价值，以及无需奖励的兴趣。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: properties unchanged by sample size, and the behaviour of a pure crystal.
branches.cn: 材料一面：不随样品大小改变的性质，以及纯晶体自身的行为。

branches.en: THE ANATOMICAL SIDE: muscles whose ends both lie inside the organ they move.
branches.cn: 解剖一面：两端都在所运动器官内部的肌肉。

branches.en: THE SELF-CONTAINED SIDE: curvature measured within a surface, and growth generated inside an economy.
branches.cn: 自足一面：在曲面内部测得的曲率，以及经济体内部产生的增长。

intro.en: Intrinsic is a Latin adverb turned adjective: intra 'within' plus secus 'alongside', with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: intrinsic 是由拉丁副词转成的形容词：intra「在内」加 secus「沿着」，再加形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Intra plus secus gives the adverb intrinsecus 'inwardly'; the adjective form, through French, is intrinsèque, taken into English as intrinsic.
latinIntro.cn: intra 加 secus 得出副词 intrinsecus「向内」；其形容词形式经法语作 intrinsèque，进入英语成为 intrinsic。

items.example: The prefix locates the quality inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把性质定位在内部。

items.example: Its earlier origin is disputed, so the compound is not fully certain.
items.exampleCN: 它更早的来源有争议，因此该复合词并非完全确证。

items.example: The adverb is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词是形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The counterpart gives the paired opposite in English.
items.exampleCN: 配对形式给出英语中的反义对照词。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把副词变成形容词。
英语加上了可量度的技术义。

items.example: The ending gives the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给出方式副词。

items.example: The suffix names the inner quality in philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀在哲学中命名「内在性」。

items.example: The longer form is now archaic.
items.exampleCN: 较长的形式如今已属古旧。

items.example: The opposite partner appears in the same technical fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个对立词出现在同一批技术领域。
