definition_zh: 口音；重音；重音符号；强调
definition_en: the way a group speaks, a stressed syllable, or special emphasis
core_image: 一句话说到某个音节时，声音轻轻往上一挑
scene: 她一张口，尾音轻轻上扬，听得出不是本地人。 His accent told us he had grown up abroad.
sceneCN: 这里的 accent 指「口音」（第 1 个义项：说话带出的地方语音特征）；句意是他的口音表明他在国外长大。

pos.zh: 口音；重音；重音符号；强调

derivatives.zh: 义为「重音的；按重音节拍的」

senses.title: A way of speaking
senses.definition: the way a group or region pronounces a language
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体或地区说话发音的方式
senses.example: His accent told us he had grown up abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他的口音表明他在国外长大。
senses.why: The Latin root cantus means song, and accent first named the tune of the voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cantus 意为歌唱，accent 最初指嗓音的调子。

senses.title: A stressed syllable
senses.definition: the stronger beat given to one syllable in a word
senses.definitionCN: 一个词中某个音节读得更强
senses.example: The accent falls on the second syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 重音落在第二个音节上。
senses.why: A raised beat in speech is a small song inside a word.
senses.whyCN: 说话时抬高的那一拍，是词里的一小段歌。

senses.title: A written mark
senses.definition: a mark placed over a letter to show its sound
senses.definitionCN: 写在字母上方以标示读音的符号
senses.example: The word carries an accent on the final e.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词最后一个 e 上带一个符号。
senses.why: The tune of the voice was written down as a small mark.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音的调子被写下来，就成了一个小符号。

senses.title: Special emphasis
senses.definition: special importance given to an idea or detail
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个想法或细节的特别重视
senses.example: The report puts the accent on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把重点放在安全上。
senses.why: A stressed beat in speech became a stressed point in argument.
senses.whyCN: 言语中加重的一拍，成了论述里被加重的一点。

senses.title: To stress a word
senses.definition: to pronounce a syllable or word more strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把某个音节或词读得更重
senses.example: Accent the first syllable in this name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名字的第一个音节要重读。
senses.why: The verb simply performs the stress that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词做的，正是名词所指的那一下加重。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin noun for song added to speech.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到表示「加在言语上的歌」的拉丁名词。

items.cn: cantus 意为歌唱、歌曲。

items.en: accentus meant a tone added to speech.
items.cn: accentus 指加在言语上的调子。

items.en: accent carried the musical sense into French.
items.cn: accent 把这个音乐性的意义带进法语。

items.en: accent entered English for the tune of the voice.
items.cn: accent 进入英语，指嗓音的调子。

items.en: it now covers regional speech, stress and written marks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖地方口音、重音与书写符号。

note.cn: 形近组是 accent 词族；近义组是别的与语音有关的词。

normalIntro.en: These hints follow cantus, the Latin word for song.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「歌」的 cantus。

normal.en: cantus means song, and accent is the song inside speech.
normal.cn: cantus 意为歌，accent 就是言语里的那点歌。

normal.en: ac- is a form of ad-, meaning added to.
normal.cn: ac- 是 ad- 的变体，意为「加到……上」。

normal.en: a regional accent is a tune learned at home.
normal.cn: 地方口音是在家里学会的调子。

normal.en: a written accent is that tune turned into a mark.
normal.cn: 书写里的重音符号，是那个调子变成了笔画。

normal.en: to accent a point is to make the voice lean on it.
normal.cn: 强调一个观点，就是让声音压在上面。

abstract.en: See a voice rising at the end of a phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话的尾音轻轻上扬。

abstract.en: Picture a small mark floating above a letter.
abstract.cn: 想象字母上方浮着一个小符号。

abstract.en: Think of a finger tapping one beat harder.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在某一拍上敲得更重。

examples.cn: 他的口音表明他在国外长大。

sensesIntro.cn: 加在言语上的调子，成了地方口音、加重的一拍、纸上的符号，以及被强调的要点。

branches.en: the tune written as a small sign
branches.cn: 被写成小符号的调子

branches.en: importance laid on an idea
branches.cn: 落在一个观点上的分量

branches.cn: 嗓音与论述都在某处加重

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix and a root about singing.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀加上一个与歌唱有关的词根。

latinIntro.en: The root cantus, song, also gives chant, canticle and incantation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cantus（歌）也生出 chant、canticle 与 incantation。

definition_zh: 充气；通气；使暴露于空气
definition_en: to introduce air into a material or substance
core_image: 园艺叉插进草坪再拔起，留下一排透气的小孔
scene: 园丁推着打孔机在草坪上来回走，泥土里冒出细孔。 They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 aerate 是「给土壤通气」（第 1 个义项：把空气引入某物）；句意为他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「通气；充气」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「充气器；打孔机」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「充了气的」

senses.title: Introduce air into soil or material
senses.definition: to force air into soil, compost or another material
senses.definitionCN: 把空气压入土壤、堆肥或其他材料中
senses.example: They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。
senses.why: Greek aer means 'air', so the verb is literally 'to put air into'.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」，所以这个动词字面上就是「把空气放进去」。

senses.title: Charge a liquid with gas
senses.definition: to add carbon dioxide or another gas to a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 往液体里加入二氧化碳或其他气体
senses.example: The bar served aerated water with strong bubbles.
senses.exampleCN: 酒吧供应气泡很足的充气水。
senses.why: Air in the first sense generalizes to any gas stirred into a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的「空气」扩展为搅入液体的任何气体。

senses.title: Expose to fresh air
senses.definition: to let fresh air move through a space or substance
senses.definitionCN: 让新鲜空气在空间或物质中流通
senses.example: Open the windows to aerate the room after painting.
senses.exampleCN: 刷完漆后开窗给房间换换气。
senses.why: Putting air in implies letting air through: the material is opened to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 「放进空气」也意味着「让空气通过」：让物质向大气敞开。

intro.en: Aerate comes from Greek aer, 'air', joined to the Latin verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: aerate 由希腊语 aer（空气）加拉丁语动词尾 -ate 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wer- is linked to words for rising air and wind.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wer- 与表示升腾之气和风的词相关联。

items.en: Aer meant 'air, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」。

items.en: Scientific Latin aeratus meant 'charged with air', coined for chemistry.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语 aeratus 意为「充了气的」，为化学而造。

items.en: English formed aerate in the eighteenth century for chemistry and brewing.
items.cn: 英语于十八世纪造出 aerate，用于化学与酿造。

items.en: The verb now spans lawns, aquariums, wines and fizzy drinks.
items.cn: 如今该动词覆盖草坪、水族箱、醒酒与气泡饮料。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same air root; the second gathers related breathing and gas words.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「空气」词根的词；第二组收与呼吸、气体相关的词。

entries.definition: Of the air or an antenna; shares Greek aer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「空中的；天线」；同享希腊语 aer 词根。

entries.definition: Tiny particles or gas in a spray; the sol- half means 'solution'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气溶胶；喷雾」；前半同为 aer，后半 sol 意为「溶液」。

entries.definition: Requiring oxygen; built on the same air root with bios, 'life'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「需氧的」；同用 air 词根加 bios（生命）。

entries.definition: To move fresh air through a space.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通风」，让空气在空间中流动。

entries.definition: To add oxygen to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供氧；加氧」。

entries.definition: To charge a drink with carbon dioxide.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使充二氧化碳」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air root and the lawn-fork scene; the abstract hooks picture bubbles and open windows.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气」词根与草坪打孔场景；抽象记忆点想象气泡与敞开的窗。

normal.en: Greek aer means 'air'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」。

normal.en: Aeration is the noun, aerator the tool.
normal.cn: aeration 是名词，aerator 是工具。

normal.en: Aerated water is full of bubbles.
normal.cn: 充气水里全是气泡。

normal.en: Aerate the lawn by punching holes.
normal.cn: 给草坪打孔就是 aerate。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks it as a verb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标明它是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a fork lifting plugs of green turf.
abstract.cn: 想象草叉撬起一块块绿草皮。

abstract.en: Picture bubbles racing up a glass of soda.
abstract.cn: 想象气泡在一杯汽水里竞相上蹿。

abstract.en: Picture a stuffy room breathing again.
abstract.cn: 想象一间闷室重新呼吸起来。

examples.en: They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
examples.cn: 他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。

examples.en: Aerate the wine for a few minutes before serving.
examples.cn: 上桌前先给红酒醒几分钟气。

examples.en: Fish-tank pumps aerate the water all night.
examples.cn: 鱼缸气泵整夜给水增氧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 air »瑞特」——空气 air 被「瑞特」地塞进去，就是充气、通气。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）→ 新拉丁语 aeratus（充气的）→ 英语 aerate；核心义是「把空气送进东西里」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from aerating soil, to charging liquids with gas, to airing out spaces.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从给土壤通气，到给液体充气，再到给空间换气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air pushed into something dense until it breathes
core.cn: 核心意象：把空气压进密实之物，让它重新呼吸

branches.en: Holes punched so roots can breathe.
branches.cn: 打好孔让根系呼吸。

branches.en: Gas stirred into water or wine.
branches.cn: 搅进水或酒里的气体。

branches.en: Windows opened to moving air.
branches.cn: 向流动空气敞开的窗。

branches.en: Both senses let stale places breathe again.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让死气之地重新吐纳。

branches.en: Fizz is this sense's everyday face.
branches.cn: 气泡水是这个义项的日常面孔。

intro.en: The word carries the Greek air root aer- with the Latin verb ending -ate, and the family gives aerial, aerosol and aerobic.
intro.cn: 这个词带着希腊语「空气」词根 aer- 与拉丁动词尾 -ate，同族词有 aerial、aerosol 与 aerobic。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer via scientific Latin aeratus is the recorded ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的祖先是从希腊语 aer 到科学拉丁语 aeratus。

definition_zh: 住宅；住所；居住
definition_en: the place where someone lives, or the fact of living there
core_image: 一扇亮着灯的窗，窗后是某人固定的家
scene: 总统官邸位于河岸边，四周有高高的围栏。 The president's residence stands by the river, surrounded by high fences.
sceneCN: 这里 residence 是「官邸；住宅」（第 1 个义项：某人居住的地方）；句意：总统官邸位于河岸边，四周有高高的围栏。

senses.title: The place where someone lives
senses.definition: the house or place in which a person lives
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住的房子或地方
senses.example: The president's residence stands by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 总统官邸位于河岸边。
senses.why: The noun names the place produced by residing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指居住这一行为所产生的场所。

senses.title: The act or period of living somewhere
senses.definition: the fact of living in a place, often used in official language
senses.definitionCN: 在某地居住的事实，常用于官方语言
senses.example: She took up residence in Paris last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年开始在巴黎居住。
senses.why: Residence can name the state of living there, not only the building.
senses.whyCN: residence 可指居住状态，而不只是建筑。

senses.title: A large impressive house
senses.definition: a large and formal house, especially an official one
senses.definitionCN: 大型而正式的住宅，尤指官邸
senses.example: The family moved to a smaller residence.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人搬进了一处较小的宅邸。
senses.why: The formal word for a home often suggests size and dignity.
senses.whyCN: 「住所」的正式说法常带有规模与体面的意味。

intro.en: Residence comes from Latin residentia, a staying behind, from residere, to remain, through Old French residence.
intro.cn: residence 来自拉丁语 residentia（停留），源于 residere（留下），经古法语 residence 进入英语。

items.en: Sedere means to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Residere means to remain behind or dwell.
items.cn: residere 意为留下、居住。

items.en: Residentia means a staying behind or a dwelling.
items.cn: residentia 意为停留、居所。

items.en: Residence means a place of dwelling.
items.cn: residence 意为居住之处。

items.en: English residence names both the act and the place of living.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，英语 residence 兼指居住行为与住所。

items.en: Modern English uses residence for homes, permits, and official dwellings.
items.cn: 现代英语中，residence 用于住宅、居留许可与官邸。

note.en: Residence is the noun of residing, and it sits near its family and near words for home and dwelling.
note.cn: residence 是 reside 的名词，与自身词族以及表示家和住所的词相邻。

entries.definition: to live in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住

entries.definition: a person who lives in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居民

entries.definition: made up of homes
entries.definitionCN: 住宅的

entries.definition: the place where someone lives
entries.definitionCN: 家

entries.definition: a building for people to live in
entries.definitionCN: 房子

entries.definition: a place where someone lives, formal
entries.definitionCN: 住所（正式）

normalIntro.en: Residence is the noun of reside: the place or fact of staying.
normalIntro.cn: residence 是 reside 的名词：停留的场所或事实。

normal.en: Take up residence means begin living somewhere.
normal.cn: take up residence 意为开始在某地居住。

normal.en: An official residence is a home provided for a leader.
normal.cn: official residence 是为领导人提供的官邸。

normal.en: Residence permit names the right to live in a country.
normal.cn: residence permit 指在一个国家居留的权利。

normal.en: A residence can be modest or grand.
normal.cn: 住宅可以朴素，也可以宏伟。

normal.en: Compare home: home is emotional, while residence is formal.
normal.cn: 对比 home：home 带情感，residence 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture one lit window in a dark row of houses.
abstract.cn: 想象一排黑暗的房子里，只有一扇窗亮着。

abstract.en: Imagine an address written carefully on a form.
abstract.cn: 想象地址被工整地写在表格上。

abstract.en: Think of a door key kept for many years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把保存多年的门钥匙。

examples.en: The president's residence stands by the river.
examples.cn: 总统官邸位于河岸边。

examples.en: She took up residence in Paris last year.
examples.cn: 她去年开始在巴黎居住。

examples.en: The family moved to a smaller residence.
examples.cn: 这家人搬进了一处较小的宅邸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reside + ence」——居住这件事或这个地方，就是住所；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ residere（留下、居住）→ residentia（停留、居所）→ 古法语 residence → 现代英语 residence。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names a dwelling, then the state of living there, and finally a large formal home such as an official one.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词先指住所，再指居住状态，最后指大型正式住宅，如官邸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit window that marks one person's fixed home.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇亮着的窗，标记着一个人固定的家。

branches.en: The physical home is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 物理住所，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: The act of living there appears in official phrases.
branches.cn: 居住行为出现在官方短语中。

branches.en: A grand house adds dignity to the same word.
branches.cn: 宏伟住宅为同一个词增添体面意味。

branches.en: The building and the fact of living there depend on each other.
branches.cn: 建筑与居住事实彼此依存。

branches.en: Official residence joins the legal and the grand senses.
branches.cn: official residence 把法律含义与宏伟含义结合起来。

intro.en: Residence is an English -ence noun built on the Latin verb residere.
intro.cn: residence 是建立在拉丁动词 residere 上的英语 -ence 名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit, residere means to remain, and residentia means a dwelling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，residere 意为留下，residentia 意为居所。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of remaining.

definition_zh: 激怒；使恼火；使失去耐心；加剧（书面，指病情或麻烦）
definition_en: to make someone extremely annoyed and frustrated, especially by repeated provocation
core_image: 一块粗糙的石头反复摩擦绳子，把绳子一点点磨起毛
scene: 深夜的会议室里，同一个问题被反复追问，主管终于压不住火气。 After the third round of questions, the same answer began to exasperate the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 exasperate 是「激怒、使恼火」（第 1 个义项：使人非常生气）；句意：问到第三轮时，同样的回答开始让整个团队恼火。

pos.zh: 激怒；使恼火；使失去耐心

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -tion 构成名词，义为「恼怒；愤懑」
现在分词转形容词，义为「令人恼火的」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被激怒的；又气又无奈的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「恼火地」

senses.title: To make someone very angry
senses.definition: to make a person extremely annoyed, often so that the anger shows in the voice or face
senses.definitionCN: 使人极为恼火，往往气得在声音或脸色上表露出来
senses.example: Slow traffic and endless forms exasperate most drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的车流和没完没了的表格让大多数司机恼火。
senses.why: Latin asper means rough, and exasperare meant to make a surface rough; to exasperate a person is to roughen the temper until it turns harsh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 asper 意为「粗糙」，exasperare 本义是「使表面变粗糙」；激怒一个人，就是把他的脾气磨粗，直到语气变硬。

senses.title: To wear down the patience of someone
senses.titleCN: 使失去耐心；使无可奈何
senses.definition: to exhaust the patience of a person through many small repeated irritations rather than one large offence
senses.definitionCN: 不是一次大的冒犯，而是许多小事反复消耗掉一个人的耐心
senses.example: The endless questions of the child at bedtime exasperated his tired mother.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子临睡前没完没了的问题，让疲惫的母亲失去了耐心。
senses.why: The verb pictures a process rather than a blow, so the object is not struck once but worn thin until patience runs out.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词描绘的是一段过程而不是一次打击，所以对象不是被击中一次，而是被磨薄到耐心耗尽。

senses.title: To be left helplessly annoyed
senses.titleCN: 被弄得又气又无奈（多用被动）
senses.definition: used in the passive, to describe a settled state of frustrated anger with no easy outlet
senses.definitionCN: 多用于被动语态，描述一种找不到出口、已经定型的恼怒与无奈
senses.example: She was exasperated by the refusal of the council to answer her letters.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会始终不回复她的信，她被弄得又气又无奈。
senses.why: In the passive the participle names the end point of the roughening, so the sentence reports a state that has already set in, not an act in progress.
senses.whyCN: 在被动语态里，分词指的是「磨粗」这一过程的结果，所以句子陈述的是一种已经形成的心态，而不是正在进行的动作。

senses.title: To make a bad condition worse
senses.titleCN: 加剧；使（病情、麻烦）恶化（书面，少见）
senses.definition: to intensify an illness, a wound, or a difficulty; a formal and now uncommon use
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、伤口或困难加重；书面语用法，如今已少见
senses.example: Cold winds exasperated the old wound in his leg.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风让他腿上的旧伤更加难熬。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the image: roughening a surface makes a sore place worse, so the same verb once meant to aggravate a disease.
senses.whyCN: 这是意象中最古老的一层：把表面磨粗会让原本疼痛的地方更难受，所以这个动词过去也能表示「使病情加重」。

intro.en: Exasperate comes from Latin exasperare, to make rough, built from ex- and asper, rough; English took the verb in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: exasperate 来自拉丁语 exasperare（使变粗糙），由 ex- 与 asper（粗糙）构成；英语在十六世纪引入这个动词。

items.en: Asper is a Latin adjective meaning rough, harsh, or uneven.
items.cn: asper 是拉丁语形容词，意为粗糙的、严厉的、不平整的。

items.en: Ex- adds the idea of thoroughly or out, and asperare means to make rough.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 加上「彻底、向外」的意思，asperare 意为使变粗糙。

items.en: Exasperare means to roughen and, in transferred use, to provoke or irritate.
items.cn: exasperare 意为使粗糙，引申用法则是挑动、激怒。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the 1500s with the sense of provoking anger.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，义为挑起怒火。

items.en: Later English keeps both the everyday sense of annoying and the older medical sense of worsening a condition.
items.cn: 后来的英语同时保留了「使人恼火」的日常义和「使病情加重」的古老医学义。

note.en: Exasperate belongs to the rough family of asper, and stands at the strong end of the anger words.
note.cn: exasperate 属于 asper（粗糙）这个词族，在表示「生气」的词里处于强烈的一端。

entries.definition: the feeling of being extremely annoyed
entries.definitionCN: 恼怒；愤懑

entries.definition: extremely annoying
entries.definitionCN: 令人恼火的

entries.definition: harshness of manner or tone
entries.definitionCN: （态度或语气的）严厉、粗硬

entries.definition: to make someone slightly angry
entries.definitionCN: 使恼火；使烦躁

entries.definition: to make someone extremely angry
entries.definitionCN: 使大怒

entries.definition: to make someone a little angry
entries.definitionCN: 使烦恼；惹恼

normalIntro.en: Exasperate keeps the Latin word for rough, so the picture is a temper rubbed the wrong way.
normalIntro.cn: exasperate 保留了拉丁语里「粗糙」这个词，所以画面是被逆向摩擦的脾气。

normal.en: Asper in Latin means rough, and exasperate keeps that roughness inside the anger.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 asper 意为粗糙，exasperate 把这份粗糙留在了怒火里。

normal.en: Add the prefix ex- and the verb moves from making rough to making angry.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 ex-，动词就从「使粗糙」走到「使生气」。

normal.en: The noun is exasperation, the worn-out feeling left after repeated annoyance.
normal.cn: 名词是 exasperation，指反复被烦之后留下的那种疲惫的恼怒。

normal.en: Say exasperated by, exasperated at, or exasperated with to name the cause.
normal.cn: 说 exasperated by、exasperated at 或 exasperated with 都能点出原因。

normal.en: Compare irritate: irritate is milder, exasperate is the worn-down stronger end.
normal.cn: 对比 irritate：irritate 较轻，exasperate 是被磨到尽头、更强烈的那一端。

abstract.en: Picture a rough stone dragging across a rope until the fibres stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象一块粗石在绳子上拖过，直到纤维全都竖起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a tap dripping on the same spot all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一个水龙头整夜滴在同一处。

abstract.en: Think of a door that will not open however hard you push.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，无论怎么推都推不开。

examples.en: The constant noise from the building site exasperated the whole street.
examples.cn: 工地不断的噪音让整条街的人都恼火。

examples.en: He was exasperated by the endless delays at the airport.
examples.cn: 机场没完没了的延误把他弄得又气又无奈。

examples.en: Nothing exasperates her more than a meeting with no agenda.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一场没有议程的会议更让她恼火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个在死逼」——被人一步步逼到火气上来，就是被激怒；拆开看是 ex 加 asper（粗糙），粗糙的摩擦让人恼火，这一半才是词源线索，谐音部分只是辅助。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、彻底）+ asper（粗糙）→ exasperare（使粗糙、激怒）→ 拉丁语 exasperatus → 英语 exasperate，核心义「把脾气磨粗糙」。

sensesIntro.en: Exasperate starts as making rough, becomes making angry, then wearing patience thin, then naming a helpless state, and finally worsening a condition.
sensesIntro.cn: exasperate 从「使粗糙」出发，先指使人发火，再指把耐心磨薄，继而指一种无奈的心态，最后指使病情或麻烦加重。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stone rubbing a rope until it frays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块粗糙的石头反复摩擦绳子，直到绳子起毛。

branches.en: Roughness turned against a person is the core sense of open anger.
branches.cn: 把粗糙施加到人身上，就是表露在外的怒火这一核心义。

branches.en: Friction repeated many times wears patience down instead of striking once.
branches.cn: 反复的摩擦不是一次打击，而是把耐心一点点磨掉。

branches.en: The passive result is a settled state of helpless anger.
branches.cn: 被动语态的结果，是一种已经定型的无奈怒火。

branches.en: The old medical use keeps the literal idea of making a sore place rougher.
branches.cn: 古老的医学用法保留了「让疼痛处更粗糙」这一字面意思。

branches.en: Both senses share the same picture of a temper being rubbed the wrong way.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一幅画面：脾气被逆向摩擦。

intro.en: Exasperate is built from the Latin prefix ex- and asper, rough, with English suffixes forming the noun and the two adjectives.
intro.cn: exasperate 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与 asper（粗糙）构成，英语再用后缀造出名词和两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin asper means rough, and exasperare means to make rough and, by transfer, to provoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 asper 意为粗糙，exasperare 意为使粗糙，引申为挑动、激怒。

items.example: The prefix ex- strengthens the verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 加强了动词的语气。
asper 提供粗糙的表面这一意象。

items.example: Asperare turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: asperare 把这个形容词变成动作。

items.example: Exasperare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: exasperare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Exasperatus gives the passive sense of the result.
items.exampleCN: exasperatus 提供表示结果的被动含义。

items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词干构成动词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate carries the Latin stem into English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干带入英语。

items.example: Exasperate keeps the learned tone of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: exasperate 保留了拉丁动词的书面语色彩。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的词尾

definition_zh: 修正；修订；修正案；（法律文件的）更改；（土壤）改良剂；改过自新
definition_en: a change made to correct or improve something, especially a formal change to a law or document, or the act of removing faults from something
core_image: 把条文里那处缺陷挖掉、补正，让文本重新站直
scene: 议事厅里，一名议员把一张纸推到桌子中央，提议把「十八岁投票」写进宪法。 In the chamber, a member pushes a sheet of paper to the centre of the table and proposes an amendment that would let eighteen-year-olds vote.
sceneCN: 这里 amendment 是「宪法修正案」（第 2 个义项：对宪法或法律的正式修改）；句意：议事厅里，一名议员把纸推到桌子中央，提出一项允许十八岁者投票的宪法修正案。场景要点：议事厅的长桌、推到中央的纸页、纸上的编号、议员举起的手。

pos.zh: 修正；修订；修正案；（土壤）改良剂；改过自新

senses.title: Making something better by removing faults
senses.definition: the act of correcting or improving something that is faulty or imperfect
senses.definitionCN: 纠正或改进有缺陷、不完美之事的行为
senses.example: The amendment of the manuscript took longer than writing it.
senses.exampleCN: 修订这份手稿花的时间比写它还长。
senses.why: The earliest sense, recorded in the early 13th century, is simply 'betterment, improvement'. Latin emendare is ex- 'out' plus menda 'fault', so making better begins with taking a fault out, not with putting something in.
senses.whyCN: 最早义项记录于 13 世纪早期，就是“改善、变好”。拉丁语 emendare 是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”，所以“变好”的起点是把缺陷拿出去，而不是把东西放进去。

senses.title: A formal change to a constitution or law
senses.titleCN: 对宪法或法律的正式修改
senses.definition: an official change to a constitution, statute, or legal instrument, made according to established procedure
senses.definitionCN: 依照既定程序对宪法、成文法或法律文书作出的正式更改
senses.example: The First Amendment protects freedom of speech and of the press.
senses.exampleCN: 第一修正案保护言论与出版自由。
senses.why: A constitution is treated as a text with possible faults or gaps. Once the correction must pass a fixed procedure, the act of removing the fault becomes a numbered public document called an amendment.
senses.whyCN: 宪法被当作一份可能有缺陷或空白的文本。当纠正必须经过固定程序时，“去掉缺陷”的行为就变成一份编号的公开文件，称为 amendment。

senses.title: A proposed change to a bill
senses.definition: a change proposed to a bill during debate, by a member or a committee, before it becomes law
senses.definitionCN: 法案在辩论期间由议员或委员会提出、在其成为法律之前的更改
senses.example: The committee tabled an amendment to cut the proposed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提出一项修正案，要求削减拟议预算。
senses.why: Here the fault is not yet in a finished law but in a draft. The amendment is the correction offered while the text is still open, which is why it is often a proposal rather than a settled change.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺陷还不在已生效的法律里，而在草案里。修正案是在文本仍然敞开时提出的纠正，因此它往往是一项提案，而不是已经落定的更改。

senses.title: Correction of an error in legal process
senses.titleCN: 对法律程序错误的更正
senses.definition: in law, the correction of an error in a writ, pleading, or court process
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，对令状、诉状或法院程序中的错误进行更正
senses.example: The court allowed an amendment of the writ to correct the defendant's name.
senses.exampleCN: 法院允许修改令状，以更正被告的姓名。
senses.why: The sense 'correction of error in a legal process' is recorded about 1600, and 'alteration of a writ or bill to remove its faults' in the 1690s. The fault is now procedural, and the amendment is the official act that removes it.
senses.whyCN: “更正法律程序中的错误”这一义项约记录于 1600 年，而“更改令状或法案以去掉其缺陷”记录于 17 世纪 90 年代。这里的缺陷是程序性的，修正就是去掉它的正式行为。

senses.title: A change to a contract or agreement
senses.definition: a formal change to the terms of a contract, lease, or agreement, usually signed by all parties
senses.definitionCN: 对合同、租约或协议条款的正式更改，通常由各方签署
senses.example: Both parties signed an amendment extending the lease by two years.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签署了一份修正协议，把租期延长两年。
senses.why: A contract is a text whose terms must fit reality. When reality changes, the mismatch is treated as a fault in the document, and the amendment restores the fit.
senses.whyCN: 合同是一份条款必须贴合现实的文本。现实一变，不匹配就被当作文件里的缺陷，而 amendment 恢复这种贴合。

senses.title: A textual revision before publication
senses.definition: a correction or revision made to a scholarly, technical, or literary text
senses.definitionCN: 对学术、技术或文学文本所作的更正或修订
senses.example: The journal asked for several amendments before accepting the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊在接受论文之前要求作几处修订。
senses.why: This is the domain where the old 'remove the fault' sense survives most purely. The sibling verb emend and the noun emendation are reserved for exactly this textual work, while amendment has spread to law and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这是“去掉缺陷”这一古老义项保留得最纯粹的领域。同源的动词 emend 与名词 emendation 专门用于这种文本工作，而 amendment 则扩展到了法律与制度。

senses.title: Material added to improve soil
senses.definition: a substance such as compost, lime, or gypsum added to soil to improve its condition for growing plants
senses.definitionCN: 为改善土壤种植条件而加入土壤的物质，如堆肥、石灰或石膏
senses.example: Compost is a common soil amendment in organic farming.
senses.exampleCN: 堆肥是有机农业中常见的土壤改良剂。
senses.why: This looks like the 'adding' sense, but the name comes from the purpose, not the motion: the material is called an amendment because it amends the soil, that is, removes its defects. The addition is only the means.
senses.whyCN: 这看起来像“添加”义，但名称来自目的而非动作：这种材料被称为 amendment，是因为它改良土壤，也就是去掉土壤的缺陷。添加只是手段。

senses.title: Reformation of a person's conduct
senses.definition: the correction or improvement of a person's behaviour or character, an older sense recorded around 1300
senses.definitionCN: 对一个人的行为或品性的纠正与改善，这一较古老的义项约记录于 1300 年
senses.example: The programme was designed for the amendment of young offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目是为改造年轻罪犯而设计的。
senses.why: Around 1300 the word was applied to persons as well as things: a person could be 'corrected, reformed'. The fault is now a habit or a character trait, and removing it is moral improvement.
senses.whyCN: 约 1300 年时，这个词也用于人而不只是物：人可以“被纠正、被改造”。这里的缺陷是习惯或品性，去掉它就是道德上的改善。

senses.title: An addition wearing the name of correction
senses.titleCN: 顶着“修正”之名的追加条款
senses.definition: in modern legislative usage, a provision attached to a law or bill that is formally an amendment even when it adds new material rather than repairing a fault
senses.definitionCN: 在现代立法用法中，附加到法律或法案上的条款；即使它增加新内容而非修复缺陷，形式上仍叫 amendment
senses.example: The bill was loaded with amendments that had little to do with correcting anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案被塞进了许多与纠正错误几乎无关的修正条款。
senses.why: The meaning 'to add to legislation, ostensibly to correct or improve it' is recorded from 1777. The word's form still says 'remove the fault', but practice can turn it into an addition, which is exactly where learners misread amendment as 'extra clause'.
senses.whyCN: “为立法增加内容、名义上是纠正或改进它”这一用法记录于 1777 年。词形仍在说“去掉缺陷”，但实践可以把它变成追加，这正是学习者把 amendment 误读为“额外条款”的地方。

intro.en: Amendment is amend plus -ment, and amend comes from Old French amender, from Latin emendare 'to correct, free from fault'. The Latin verb is ex- 'out' + menda 'fault, blemish', so the core is removal of a defect, not addition. The same Latin source gives emend and emendation, but those stay in the domain of textual correction, while amendment spread to law, contracts and even soil.
intro.cn: amendment 是 amend 加 -ment；amend 来自古法语 amender，再上溯拉丁语 emendare“纠正、去掉缺陷”。这个拉丁动词是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷、瑕疵”，所以核心是“去掉缺陷”，不是“添加”。同一拉丁来源还给出 emend 与 emendation，但这两个词留在文本校勘领域，而 amendment 扩展到了法律、合同甚至土壤。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'betterment, improvement'. By c.1300 it is also used of persons, meaning 'correction, reformation'. The starting point is not an added clause but a thing made better.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“改善、变好”。到 1300 年左右也用于人，意为“纠正、改造”。起点不是追加条款，而是使某物变好。

items.en: From Old French amendement 'rectification, correction; advancement, improvement', from amender 'to amend' (12c.), which could mean 'correct, set right, make better, improve'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 amendement“纠正、改正；促进、改善”，出自 amender“修正”（12 世纪），意为“纠正、摆正、使更好、改进”。

items.en: Amender goes back to Latin emendare 'to correct, free from fault', built from ex 'out' + menda, mendum 'fault, physical blemish; error'. The prepositional image is pulling the fault out of the thing.
items.cn: amender 上溯拉丁语 emendare“纠正、去掉缺陷”，由 ex“出”加 menda、mendum“缺陷、身体瑕疵；错误”构成。其介词意象是把缺陷从东西里拉出来。

items.en: Standard references trace menda to PIE *mend- 'physical defect, fault', said to be the source also of Sanskrit minda 'physical blemish', Old Irish mennar 'stain', Welsh mann 'sign, mark', and Hittite mant- 'something harming'. The set is well attested, though the exact reconstruction is not beyond dispute.
items.cn: 通行词源资料把 menda 追溯到原始印欧语 *mend-“身体缺陷、过错”，并称它也是梵语 minda“身体瑕疵”、古爱尔兰语 mennar“污点”、威尔士语 mann“记号”与赫梯语 mant-“有害之物”的来源。这组对应有充分记录，但具体构拟并非毫无争议。

items.en: The spelling with a- is unusual but early, and also appears in Provençal and Italian. In English, the senses 'repair; cure' were largely taken over by the shortened offspring mend, formed by dropping the initial a-. That is why amendment now sounds institutional while mend sounds manual.
items.cn: 带 a- 的拼写不寻常但出现很早，也见于普罗旺斯语和意大利语。在英语里，“修理；治愈”这些义项大多被缩短形式 mend 接管——它去掉了开头的 a-。因此 amendment 现在听起来偏制度，而 mend 听起来偏手工。

items.en: The legal sense 'correction of error in a legal process' is c.1600, and 'alteration of a writ or bill to remove its faults' is the 1690s. The meaning 'to add to legislation, ostensibly to correct or improve it' is recorded from 1777, which marks the drift toward 'added clause'. Modern soil amendment is named for the improvement it brings, not for the act of adding.
items.cn: 法律义“更正法律程序中的错误”约在 1600 年，“更改令状或法案以去掉缺陷”在 17 世纪 90 年代。“为立法增加内容、名义上纠正或改进它”的用法记录于 1777 年，这标志着向“追加条款”的漂移。现代 soil amendment 是因它带来的改良而得名，而不是因“添加”这个动作。

note.en: The first group separates amendment from the verb it comes from, the plural noun amends, and the scholarly sibling emend; the second compares words that also name changes but do not share the 'remove a fault' core.
note.cn: 第一组把 amendment 与它的源动词、复数名词 amends、以及学术领域的同源词 emend 分开；第二组比较同样表示“改动”、却不含“去掉缺陷”核心的词。

entries.definition: to correct or improve a text, law, or situation. It is the verb behind amendment; the noun names the act or the resulting document.
entries.definitionCN: 纠正或改进文本、法律或状况。它是 amendment 背后的动词；名词指行为或由此产生的文件。

entries.definition: in the phrase make amends, compensation for a wrong done. It looks like the plural of amend but functions as a fixed noun meaning reparation.
entries.definitionCN: 用于 make amends，意为对造成的过错作出补偿。它看起来像 amend 的复数，但实际是表示“补偿”的固定名词。

entries.definition: to correct errors in a text, especially by scholarly editing. It shares Latin emendare with amend but is restricted to textual criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 校订文本中的错误，尤指学术编辑。它与 amend 共享拉丁语 emendare，但只限用于文本校勘。

entries.definition: a scholarly correction to a text, or the act of making one. It is the technical counterpart of amendment in textual criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本的学术性校正，或作出这种校正的行为。它是 amendment 在文本校勘领域的技术对应词。

entries.definition: a general re-examination and change of a text or plan. Revision can rework the whole, while an amendment usually targets a specific fault or clause.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本或计划的整体重新审视与改动。revision 可以重做整体，而 amendment 通常针对某一缺陷或条款。

entries.definition: the act of making something wrong right. Correction is narrower and more factual; a legal amendment can be formal even when nothing is strictly wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 把错误改对的行为。correction 更窄、更偏事实；法律上的 amendment 即使没有严格意义上的错误也可以是正式程序。

entries.definition: a change of any kind, with no implication that the result is better. Alteration is neutral, while amendment carries the purpose of removing a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 任何形式的改动，不暗示结果更好。alteration 是中性的，而 amendment 带有“去掉缺陷”的目的。

entries.definition: material added at the end of a document to supplement it. An addendum adds without rewriting; an amendment alters existing wording.
entries.definitionCN: 附加在文件末尾以补充内容的材料。addendum 只追加、不改写；amendment 则改动现有措辞。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ex- 'out' plus menda 'fault', the amend/emend family, and the shortened mend. No invented 'add' meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”、amend/emend 词族，以及缩短形式 mend。不编造“添加”的意思。

normal.en: Latin emendare is ex- 'out' + menda 'fault'. Amendment is literally 'fault-out', the removal of a defect.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 emendare 是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”。amendment 字面上就是“把缺陷拿出去”。

normal.en: Mend is the shortened child of amend: the same word lost its first a-. That is why you mend a sock but amend a law.
normal.cn: mend 是 amend 缩短后的子嗣：同一个词丢掉了开头的 a-。所以你补袜子用 mend，改法律用 amend。

normal.en: Emend and emendation stay with manuscripts; amendment moved into law, contracts and soil.
normal.cn: emend 与 emendation 留在手稿校勘里；amendment 则走进了法律、合同和土壤。

normal.en: Soil amendment is named for the improvement it brings to the soil, even though you physically add it.
normal.cn: soil amendment 是因它给土壤带来的改良而得名，尽管你实际上是把东西加进去。

normal.en: The modern political 'amendment' can be an added clause, but the word still pretends to be a correction: that gap is the trap.
normal.cn: 现代政治中的 amendment 可能是追加条款，但这个词仍假装自己是在纠错：这个落差正是陷阱。

abstract.en: Picture a crack in a stone step. Amendment is not a new slab laid on top; it is the work of digging out the bad piece and making the step level again.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上有一道裂缝。amendment 不是在上面铺一块新石板，而是把坏掉的一块挖出来、让台阶重新平整。

abstract.en: The same repair can be done to a sentence, a law, a contract or a person's conduct. What changes is the material, not the gesture.
abstract.cn: 同一种修补可以施于句子、法律、合同或一个人的行为。改变的是材料，不是动作。

abstract.en: When the repair is written down and voted on, it becomes a numbered document. When it merely adds, the name survives but the gesture has changed.
abstract.cn: 当修补被写下来并付诸表决，它就变成一份编号文件；当它只是追加时，名字留了下来，动作却已经变了。

examples.en: The senate passed an amendment to the housing law.
examples.cn: 参议院通过了一项住房法修正案。

examples.en: We signed a short amendment to the contract last Friday.
examples.cn: 上周五我们签署了一份简短的合同修订协议。

examples.en: The editor suggested three amendments to the second chapter.
examples.cn: 编辑建议对第二章作三处修订。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿门得门」——阿门牧师把写错的条文改得端正，再推门进去宣读 → amendment 修正、修正案

root: 来自古法语 amendement，上溯 amender 与拉丁语 emendare“去掉缺陷”，字面是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”，核心是“把缺陷拿掉”，而非“添加”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of amendment, all one gesture: a fault is found and taken out. The material can be a manuscript, a constitution, a bill, a writ, a contract, soil or a person's conduct; only in the modern legislative drift does the gesture turn into addition.
sensesIntro.cn: amendment 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：发现缺陷并把它拿出去。材料可以是手稿、宪法、法案、令状、合同、土壤或一个人的行为；只有现代立法的漂移让这个动作变成了追加。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faulty piece is dug out so the whole can stand correct.
core.cn: 核心意象：把坏掉的一块挖出来，让整体重新站正。

branches.en: THINGS AND PERSONS: a manuscript or a character can both be made better by removing what is wrong.
branches.cn: 物与人：手稿和品性都可以通过去掉错误之处而变好。

branches.en: LAW AND LEGISLATURE: a constitution is amended by procedure, and a bill is amended while it is still a draft.
branches.cn: 法律与立法：宪法依程序被修正，法案在仍是草案时被修正。

branches.en: DOCUMENTS: a writ, a contract and a scholarly text each have faults that must be officially removed.
branches.cn: 文件：令状、合同与学术文本各有必须正式去掉的缺陷。

branches.en: SOIL: the material is named for the improvement it brings, not for the act of adding it.
branches.cn: 土壤：这种材料因带来的改良而得名，而不是因添加的动作而得名。

branches.en: DRIFT: a clause may be attached purely to add, yet it still travels under the name of correction.
branches.cn: 漂移：条款可能纯粹为追加而附加，却仍顶着“纠正”的名字行走。

intro.en: Amendment is a transparent English derivative: amend + -ment. The base verb came into English from Old French, and its Latin core is ex- 'out' + menda 'fault'. English then adds -ment, -able, -atory and the negative un- to the finished stem, while the same Latin source also enters through emend and emendation.
intro.cn: amendment 是一个透明的英语派生词：amend + -ment。基础动词经古法语进入英语，其拉丁内核是 ex-“出”加 menda“缺陷”。英语随后在成品词干上加 -ment、-able、-atory 和否定前缀 un-，而同一拉丁来源还通过 emend 与 emendation 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is emendare 'to correct, free from fault', menda/mendum 'fault, blemish', and the preposition ex 'out'. Menda is not related to English mend as a separate root; mend is simply amend with its first syllable lost.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 emendare“纠正、去掉缺陷”、menda/mendum“缺陷、瑕疵”，以及介词 ex“出”。menda 与英语 mend 并非两个独立词根；mend 只是丢掉了第一个音节的 amend。

items.meaning: the act of correcting, or the corrected clause itself
items.meaningCN: 修正行为，或修正后的条款本身（-ment 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The amendment was accepted without debate.
items.exampleCN: 该修正案未经辩论就被接受了。

items.structure: Old French amender < Latin emendare (ex- out + menda fault)
items.meaning: to remove faults from something, to correct
items.example: They agreed to amend the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 他们同意修订这项条约。

items.meaning: compensation for a wrong, in make amends
items.meaningCN: （make amends）补偿；赔罪（-s 构成的固定名词）
items.example: He tried to make amends for the damage.
items.exampleCN: 他试图为造成的损害作出补偿。

items.meaning: able to be corrected or changed
items.meaningCN: 可修正的；可修订的（-able 表示能够）
items.example: The draft is still amendable at this stage.
items.exampleCN: 草案在这个阶段仍可修订。

items.meaningCN: 修正性的；起修改作用的（-atory 构成形容词）
items.example: The amendatory clause changed the payment date.
items.exampleCN: 这条修正性条款改变了付款日期。

items.meaningCN: 未修正的；未经修改的（un- 否定 + -ed 形容词）
items.example: The unamended text still contains the error.
items.exampleCN: 未修订的文本仍含有那个错误。

items.structure: e- (ex-, out) + mend(um) (fault) — same Latin source
items.meaning: to correct a text by scholarly editing
items.meaningCN: 校订文本；勘正（同源，限于文本校勘）
items.example: The editor emended the disputed line.
items.exampleCN: 编辑勘正了那行有争议的文字。

items.meaning: a scholarly correction to a text
items.meaningCN: 校勘；勘正（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The new edition lists every emendation.
items.exampleCN: 新版列出了每一处校勘。

items.structure: shortened from amend by loss of the initial a- (aphetic form)
items.meaningCN: 修补；缝补（amendment 的缩短亲族，多用于具体物件）
items.example: She mended the torn sleeve herself.
items.exampleCN: 她自己缝好了破了的袖子。

items.example: The emendatory notes fill thirty pages.
items.exampleCN: 校订注释占了三页篇幅。

definition_zh: 区分；分化；差异化；（数学）微分；分层
definition_en: the act of telling things apart, the process by which things become unlike, or the mathematical operation of finding a derivative
core_image: 一条原本同质的线分成两支：细胞、产品、课程各自长出不同的形状
scene: 显微镜下，一个细胞分裂成两个形状不同的细胞。 Under the microscope one cell divides into two cells of different shapes, and the observer writes differentiation in the notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 differentiation 是「细胞分化」（第 3 个义项：生物学上细胞变为不同形态与功能）；句意：显微镜下，一个细胞分裂成两个形状不同的细胞，观察者在记录本上写下「分化」。图中可辨识物件：显微镜、培养皿、两支不同形状的细胞、记录本。

collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的区分

senses.title: Telling two things apart
senses.definition: the act of recognizing or stating the difference between two or more things
senses.definitionCN: 识别或说明两个或更多事物之间差别的行为
senses.example: The test rewards fine differentiation between closely related species.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试奖励对近缘物种的精细区分。
senses.why: The Latin verb differre meant 'to carry apart'. Differentiation is the mental act of carrying two things apart until the gap between them is visible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 differre 意为“分开搬运”。differentiation 就是把两样东西在头脑中搬开、直到它们之间的缝隙看得见的行为。

senses.title: The process of becoming unlike
senses.definition: the process by which something develops qualities that separate it from others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 某物发展出使其区别于同类之特性的过程
senses.example: Regional dialects show gradual differentiation over centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 地区方言在数百年间逐渐分化。
senses.why: Here the word names a process rather than an act of judgment. Two things start alike and drift apart; the -ation suffix makes the drift itself the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名的不是判断行为，而是一个过程。两样东西起初相似，慢慢漂开；-ation 后缀使这段漂移本身成为名词。

senses.title: Cells taking on special roles
senses.definition: in biology, the process by which a less specialized cell becomes a distinct cell type
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中未特化的细胞变成特定细胞类型的过程
senses.example: Stem cell differentiation produces muscle, nerve and bone cells.
senses.exampleCN: 干细胞分化产生肌肉、神经与骨细胞。
senses.why: A stem cell carries the same instructions as every other cell. Differentiation is what carries one copy of those instructions down a single path, so the cell stops being interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 干细胞携带的指令与其他细胞相同。分化就是把其中一份指令搬上一条特定路径，使这个细胞不再可互换。

senses.title: Making a product stand out
senses.definition: in marketing, the design of a product or brand so that buyers perceive it as distinct from rivals
senses.definitionCN: 营销中把产品或品牌设计得让买家觉得它不同于竞争者
senses.example: The firm relies on differentiation rather than low prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠差异化而非低价取胜。
senses.why: The verb differre also means 'to defer, to set apart'. A marketer sets a product apart from the shelf around it, and the noun names that deliberate setting-apart.
senses.whyCN: 动词 differre 也有“推迟、置于一旁”的意思。营销者把产品从四周的货架上“置开”，这个名词就命名这种刻意的分离。

senses.title: Teaching different levels in one class
senses.definition: in education, the adaptation of tasks and materials to learners of different readiness levels
senses.definitionCN: 教育中为不同准备水平的学习者调整任务与材料
senses.example: Curriculum differentiation lets advanced students move ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 分层课程让进度快的学生继续向前。
senses.why: A single class is treated as a set of groups rather than one mass. The word transfers the biological image of branching paths into the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 一个班级被当作一组组人，而不是一团人。这个词把生物学的“分岔路径”意象搬进了课堂。

senses.title: The derivative in calculus
senses.definition: in mathematics, the operation of finding the rate at which a function changes
senses.definitionCN: 数学中求函数变化率的运算
senses.example: Differentiation of that curve gives its slope at every point.
senses.exampleCN: 对那条曲线求微分，就得到它在每一点的斜率。
senses.why: A difference is a gap between two values. Differentiation shrinks that gap toward zero and asks what ratio survives; the word keeps the original 'difference' at its centre.
senses.whyCN: difference 是两个值之间的间隙。微分把这个间隙缩到趋近于零，再看还剩下什么比值；这个词的中心始终是“差”。

senses.title: Magma splitting into rock types
senses.definition: in geology, the process by which a single magma body separates into chemically distinct melts or rocks
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中单一岩浆体分离成化学成分不同的熔体或岩石的过程
senses.example: Magmatic differentiation explains why one volcano erupts several rock types.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆分异解释了一座火山为何喷出多种岩石。
senses.why: One parent melt is carried apart into several fractions as minerals crystallize out. The geological sense is the laboratory version of 'becoming unlike'.
senses.whyCN: 一个母岩浆随着矿物结晶被“搬成”几个部分。这个地质义就是“变得不同”在实验室里的版本。

senses.title: Society splitting into roles
senses.definition: in sociology, the division of a society into groups and roles with distinct functions
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中社会分成功能不同的群体与角色的过程
senses.example: Urban growth brought sharper social differentiation.
senses.exampleCN: 城市增长带来更明显的社会分化。
senses.why: Modern societies do not do the same work with the same people. Differentiation names the branching of tasks, and with it the branching of identities.
senses.whyCN: 现代社会不再由同一批人做同样的工作。differentiation 命名的是任务的不断分岔，以及随之而来的身份分岔。

senses.title: Parts specializing inside a system
senses.definition: in systems theory and organization, the specialization of parts that once performed a common function
senses.definitionCN: 系统论与组织理论中原本承担共同功能的各部分走向专门化
senses.example: Biological and organizational systems both gain efficiency through differentiation.
senses.exampleCN: 生物系统与组织系统都通过功能分化提高效率。
senses.why: The counterpart of integration: a system splits into specialized parts that must then be coordinated. The word here measures internal specialization, not difference from outsiders.
senses.whyCN: 它是 integration（整合）的对立面：系统分裂成专门化的部分，随后必须被协调。这里的词衡量的是内部分工，而不是与外部者的差异。

intro.en: Differentiation is a Latin verb plus a Latin noun suffix: differre 'to carry apart', its noun differentia 'a difference', the verb differentiate, and finally -ation. English took the verb from French in the 19th century and built the noun on top of it.
intro.cn: differentiation 是拉丁动词加拉丁名词后缀：differre“分开搬运”，其名词 differentia“差异”，动词 differentiate，最后加 -ation。英语在 19 世纪从法语借入动词，再在其上造出名词。

items.en: The root *bher- meant 'to carry'. It supplies Latin ferre and English bear, and it is the second half of differre, 'to carry apart'.
items.cn: 词根 *bher- 意为“携带”。它给出拉丁语 ferre 与英语 bear，也是 differre“分开搬运”的后半部分。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry' gave differre, 'to carry apart, to differ, to defer'. Its noun differentia named a difference, and the adjective differens named 'different'.
items.cn: dis-“分开”加 ferre“搬运”构成 differre，意为“搬开、相异、推迟”。其名词 differentia 指差异，形容词 differens 指“不同的”。

items.en: The suffix -atio built process nouns from verbs, as in formatio and creatio. Attached to a Latin-derived verb, it yields an English -ation noun naming the process or its result.
items.cn: 后缀 -atio 从动词造出过程名词，如 formatio、creatio。加在拉丁来源的动词上，就得到英语的 -ation 名词，指过程或其结果。

items.en: Old French differencier carried the verb into Middle English as differencien. The noun differentiation appears later, modelled directly on Latin differentia plus -ation.
items.cn: 古法语 differencier 把动词带入中古英语作 differencien。名词 differentiation 出现得更晚，直接仿照拉丁 differentia 加 -ation 构成。

items.en: Calculus gave the word its technical sense: differentiation is the operation inverse to integration. The term spread from French and German textbooks into English in the early 19th century.
items.cn: 微积分赋予这个词技术义：differentiation 是 integration 的逆运算。该术语在 19 世纪初从法语与德语教材传入英语。

items.en: Cell differentiation and social differentiation extend the same image of branching to tissues and to societies. The word now covers both a judgement and a natural process.
items.cn: 细胞分化与社会分化把同一“分岔”意象扩展到组织与社会。这个词现在同时覆盖判断行为与自然过程。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the adjective and the noun that all sit on the same Latin base. The meaning group compares words about difference, separation and specialization.
note.cn: 形近组区分同一拉丁词基上的动词、形容词与名词；词义组比较表示差异、分离与专门化的词。

entries.definition: to tell apart, to make different, or to find a derivative. It is the verb that lies behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 区分、使不同或求导。它是名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: the state of being unlike, or the amount by which two numbers differ. It names the gap, not the process of making one.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的状态，或两数相差的量。它指缝隙本身，而不是制造缝隙的过程。

entries.definition: relating to a difference, or a small amount by which values change. In maths it is the infinitesimal increment.
entries.definitionCN: 与差异有关的，或数值变化的微小量。数学中指无穷小增量。

entries.definition: a difference explicitly recognized or a mark of quality. It stresses the line drawn, while differentiation stresses the process of drawing it.
entries.definitionCN: 被明确认识到的差别，或优异的标志。它强调画出的那条线，而 differentiation 强调画线的过程。

entries.definition: the act of concentrating on one field or function. It is the result of differentiation in biology and in organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 集中于某一领域或功能的行为。它是生物学与组织中分化的结果。

entries.definition: the process of separating and going in different directions. It describes the paths, while differentiation describes the emerging difference.
entries.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向发展的过程。它描述路径，而 differentiation 描述显现出的差异。

entries.definition: the ability to see fine differences, or unfair treatment. It is close to sense 01 but carries a social judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 看出细微差别的能力，或指不公平对待。它接近第 1 义项，但带有社会判断。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from differre, 'carry apart', and let the branching image cover cells, products and courses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 differre“分开搬运”搭起这个词，再用分岔意象覆盖细胞、产品与课程。

normal.en: See dis- + ferre: to carry apart. Differentiation is the carrying-apart made into a noun.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 ferre：分开搬运。differentiation 就是“搬开”这个动作变成名词。

normal.en: Picture one stem splitting into two branches: biology calls that cell differentiation.
normal.cn: 想象一根主干分成两枝：生物学把这叫细胞分化。

normal.en: In marketing, the same split happens on a shelf: your product takes its own branch.
normal.cn: 在营销中，同一种分岔发生在货架上：你的产品长出自己的一枝。

normal.en: Connect the maths sense to difference: a derivative measures how fast one value differs from the next.
normal.cn: 把数学义连到 difference：导数衡量一个值相对下一个值变化多快。

normal.en: Remember the pair: differentiation splits, integration joins.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：differentiation 拆开，integration 合拢。

abstract.en: Keep one shape in mind: a single trunk becoming a tree of distinct branches. Every sense is that shape.
abstract.cn: 只记一个形状：一根主干长成一棵分叉的树。每个义项都是这个形状。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a verb of distance: things are carried apart until each has its own name.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作“距离的动词”：东西被搬开，直到每样都有自己的名字。

abstract.en: Notice that the noun never fully loses 'difference': even calculus is still measuring a gap.
abstract.cn: 注意这个名词从未丢掉“difference”：连微积分也仍在测量一个间隙。

examples.en: Careful differentiation between the two hypotheses is essential.
examples.cn: 对这两个假说作出仔细区分至关重要。

examples.en: Cell differentiation turns a single fertilized egg into a whole organism.
examples.cn: 细胞分化把一个受精卵变成完整的生物体。

examples.en: Differentiation of the function gives the velocity at any moment.
examples.cn: 对该函数求微分就得到任意时刻的速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地分人先谢”：大家分地、分开、分家，先分才有 differentiation 的区分与分化。

root: 拉丁语 differre“分开搬运”（dis- 分开 + ferre 携带），名词 differentia“差异”；再经法语 differencier 进入英语作 differentiate，加拉丁名词后缀 -ation 构成 differentiation。数学的“微分”义在 19 世纪从微积分术语中固定下来。

sensesIntro.en: One Latin verb, differre, means 'to carry apart'. Everything in this entry is a version of that carrying: a mind separates two species, a stem cell takes one path, a brand is set apart on a shelf, a magma splits into fractions, a calculus operation shrinks a gap toward zero. The nine senses differ only in what is being separated and who does the separating.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拉丁动词 differre 意为“分开搬运”。本词条的一切都是这个“搬开”的版本：头脑分辨两个物种，干细胞走上一条路径，品牌在货架上被置开，岩浆分成几部分，微积分运算把间隙缩向零。九个义项的差别只在于分开的是什么、以及由谁来分。

core.en: Carrying apart: making what was one into things that are not interchangeable.
core.cn: 分开搬运：把原本是一体的东西变成不可互换的多件事物。

branches.en: Judgement and process: telling apart, and becoming unlike.
branches.cn: 判断与过程：分辨，以及逐渐变得不同。

branches.en: MATTER: cells taking roles, magma splitting into rock types.
branches.cn: 物质：细胞承担角色，岩浆分成不同岩类。

branches.en: MARKET AND SCHOOL: products set apart, lessons layered.
branches.cn: 市场与学校：产品被置开，课程被分层。

branches.en: CALCULUS: a gap shrunk toward zero.
branches.cn: 微积分：间隙被缩向零。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: societies and organizations dividing into functions.
branches.cn: 系统：社会与组织分成不同功能。

intro.en: Differentiation stacks three elements: dif- (a form of dis-), ferre 'carry', and -ation. The items below show the same base with other suffixes, and show where dis- keeps its 'apart' force.
intro.cn: differentiation 叠了三个成分：dif-（dis- 的一种形式）、ferre“携带”、-ation。下列条目展示同一词基配其他后缀，并展示 dis- 保留“分开”力量的情形。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its two nouns. They explain why a word about difference also yields a word about deferring: carrying apart and putting off are the same gesture in time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词及其两个名词。它们解释了为什么一个关于差异的词同时产生“推迟”义：在时间上把事搬开与推迟，是同一个动作。

items.meaning: the process of distinguishing or specializing
items.example: Differentiation of the two cases took hours.
items.exampleCN: 区分这两个病例花了几个小时。

items.meaning: to distinguish, to make distinct, to find a derivative
items.example: Readers must differentiate fact from opinion.
items.exampleCN: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。

items.structure: Latin differens, present participle of differre
items.example: The two samples are chemically different.
items.exampleCN: 这两个样本在化学上不同。

items.meaning: the state of being unlike; the amount between two values
items.example: The difference is only a few degrees.

items.meaning: relating to a difference; a small increment
items.meaningCN: 与差异有关的；微小增量
items.example: The differential between the two rates is small.
The accounts differ on one detail.
items.exampleCN: 这些叙述在一个细节上不同。

items.meaning: to put off to a later time
items.example: They deferred the decision until spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们把决定推迟到春天。

items.meaning: to carry back; to point to
items.example: The footnote refers to an earlier study.
items.exampleCN: 脚注指向一项更早的研究。

items.example: The data were transferred to a new drive.
The river made the valley fertile.
items.exampleCN: 这条河使河谷变得肥沃。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry apart; to differ; to defer

definition_en: a hardy cereal grass and its grain, used for food, for malting and for brewing beer and whisky
core_image: 一片金黄的麦田，风过时整片麦浪起伏
scene: 六月的田里一片金黄，风过时整片麦浪起伏。 The field of barley rippled in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 barley 是「大麦」（第 1 个义项：一种禾谷作物）；句意是大麦田在风中起伏。

senses.title: The cereal crop
senses.definition: a hardy cereal grass, Hordeum vulgare, grown for its grain
senses.definitionCN: 一种耐寒的禾谷作物，学名 Hordeum vulgare，为取麦粒而种

senses.title: Malt for brewing
senses.definition: the grain soaked and dried to make malt for beer and whisky
senses.definitionCN: 浸水发芽再烘干制成麦芽，用于啤酒与威士忌
senses.example: Malted barley gives the beer its body.
senses.exampleCN: 麦芽赋予啤酒酒体。
senses.why: Barley germinates easily, so brewers chose it over other grains.
senses.whyCN: 大麦易发芽，酿酒人因此选它而非其他谷物。

senses.title: Pearl barley as food
senses.definition: the grain polished and used in soups and stews
senses.definitionCN: 磨去外层的麦粒，用于汤与炖菜
senses.example: Add pearl barley to the soup an hour before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前一小时把珍珠麦加进汤里。
senses.why: Polishing removes the husk, leaving a round white grain called pearl barley.
senses.whyCN: 抛光去掉外壳，留下圆白的麦粒，称作珍珠麦。

senses.title: Barley drinks
senses.definition: in barley water and barley wine, drinks made from the grain
senses.definitionCN: 用于 barley water 与 barley wine 等大麦饮品
senses.example: She cooled the barley water and added lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她把大麦水放凉，再加柠檬。
senses.why: The grain names the drink, as wheat names wheat beer.
senses.whyCN: 谷物为饮品命名，正如小麦命名小麦啤酒。

intro.en: Barley is an Old English adjective that forgot it was an adjective.
intro.cn: barley 本是一个古英语形容词，后来忘了自己的词性。

items.en: The root bhares- meant barley and gave Latin far and Old English bere.
items.cn: 词根 bhares- 意为大麦，衍生出拉丁语 far 与古英语 bere。

items.en: The Germanic form bariz- carried the grain name north.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 bariz- 把这个谷物名带到北方。

items.en: Bere meant barley; barn is bere plus ern, a barley house.
items.cn: bere 意为大麦；barn 由 bere 加 ern「房屋」构成，本义「大麦屋」。

items.en: Bærlic added -lic to bere, meaning of barley.
items.cn: bærlic 在 bere 上加 -lic，意为「大麦的」。

items.en: The adjective was reanalysed as a noun, giving barley.
items.cn: 这个形容词被重新分析为名词，成为 barley。

items.en: Barley remains the brewing grain, malted into beer and whisky.
items.cn: barley 仍是酿造用谷物，制成麦芽后用于啤酒与威士忌。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ley or bar- shape; the near-meaning group lists other cereal grains.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ley 或 bar- 形状；近义组列出其他禾谷作物。

definition_zh: 在进行中；酝酿中；徒步的
definition_en: in progress or being planned; on foot, walking
core_image: 脚步已迈出：事情正在路上，肉眼可见地展开
scene: 办公室里流言四起，人人神色紧张。 Rumours of a merger were afoot long before the official announcement.
sceneCN: 这里 afoot 是「正在酝酿、进行中」（第 1 个义项：计划或活动已经在展开）；句意是合并的传言早在官方宣布之前就已四处流传。

pos.zh: 进行中的；酝酿中的（表语用法为主）

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「脚；英尺」；afoot 即 foot 的介词化组合
foot 复合名词，义为「小径；人行道」
foot 复合名词，义为「脚步声；客流」
同构词式 a- + fire，义为「燃烧着；激动不已」

senses.title: In progress or being planned
senses.definition: currently happening or being prepared, often secretly or without public confirmation
senses.definitionCN: 正在发生或正在筹划，常带有秘密进行、尚未公开的色彩
senses.example: Rumours of a merger were afoot long before the official announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 合并的传言早在官方宣布之前就已四处流传。
senses.why: The image is of feet already in motion: an undertaking has set out and cannot be seen fully yet, hence plans under way.
senses.whyCN: 意象是「脚步已经迈开」：一项行动已经上路、但全貌尚未可见，于是引申为「计划在酝酿推进中」。

senses.title: On foot; walking
senses.definition: travelling or moving on foot rather than by vehicle or horse
senses.definitionCN: 不乘车马、以双脚行进
senses.example: The pilgrims completed the last stage of their journey afoot.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者们徒步完成了旅程的最后一段。
senses.why: This is the literal layer: a- plus foot simply describes someone standing or moving on their feet.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面层：a-（处于状态）+ foot（脚），直接描写「双脚着地、以脚行进」的原始画面。

senses.title: In active circulation or existence
senses.definition: present and circulating among people, as rumours, diseases, or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指流言、疾病、观念等正在人群中流传、存在
senses.example: Several strains of flu were afoot that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天有好几种流感病毒在流行。
senses.why: What is under way is also out and about among people, so the sense extends from plans to anything circulating actively.
senses.whyCN: 「在推进」的东西同时也在人群间流转，于是词义从「计划」扩展到一切正在活跃流传的事物。

intro.en: A native English formation: the prefix a- (on, in) plus foot, first literal, then figurative.
intro.cn: 英语本土构词：前缀 a-（处于……状态）+ foot（脚），先有字面义，后生比喻义。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ped- (foot) underlies foot and its Germanic cousins.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ped-（脚）是 foot 及其日耳曼同族词的远源。

items.en: on fote meant on foot; the phrase lived as two words.
items.cn: 古英语作 on fote，意为「以脚行进」，当时仍是短语形式。

items.en: The phrase fused into afoot, keeping the walking sense and adding the sense of in progress.
items.cn: 中古英语中短语融合为 afoot，保留「徒步」义，并新增「进行中」一义。

items.en: Shakespeare uses something is afoot in the figurative sense of stirrings under way.
items.cn: 莎士比亚笔下已用 something is afoot 表示「有动静、有事酝酿」。

items.en: The figurative sense now dominates; the walking sense survives mostly in literary or set phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语中比喻义占主导；「徒步」义主要残存于书面语和固定搭配。

note.en: Afoot signals ongoing movement, often with a hint of secrecy; underway and in motion are its plain neighbours.
note.cn: afoot 强调正在推进，常带一丝隐秘色彩；underway 与 in motion 是它的平义近邻。

examples.en: Negotiations have been afoot for months without any public result.

definition_zh: 竞争力；竞争性
definition_en: the ability of a firm, industry or country to sell its goods and services against rivals
core_image: 一张赛跑成绩表上，同一个选手的排名年年前移，旁边的训练记录越写越厚
scene: 工厂的装配线旁，主管把本月成本表与对手的报价单并排贴在墙上。 Rising competitiveness in the region forced every plant to retool.
sceneCN: 这里 competitiveness 指「企业或地区相对对手的竞争能力」（第 1 个义项：企业在市场上胜过对手的能力）；句意为该地区竞争力的上升迫使每座工厂更新设备。图中可辨识物件：成本表、对手报价单、装配线、并排对比的墙面。

senses.title: A firm's ability to beat rivals
senses.definition: the capacity of one business to win customers and sales against its rivals
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业在与对手争夺顾客与销量时取胜的能力
senses.example: The firm's competitiveness rests on faster delivery rather than lower wages.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业的竞争力靠的是更快的交货，而非更低的工资。
senses.why: competitive plus -ness turns an adjective of striving into the noun for the capacity itself.
senses.whyCN: competitive 加 -ness，把表示「相争」的形容词变成表示这种能力本身的名词。

senses.title: A country's export strength
senses.definition: the ability of a national economy to sell abroad and attract investment
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济在海外销售并吸引投资的能力
senses.example: The country's export competitiveness improved after the currency was adjusted.
senses.exampleCN: 汇率调整后，该国的出口竞争力有所提升。
senses.why: governments borrowed the firm-level word and scaled it up to whole economies.
senses.whyCN: 政府借用了企业层面的词，并把它放大到整个经济体。

senses.title: The strength of a cluster or region
senses.titleCN: 产业集群或区域的实力
senses.definition: the collective ability of linked firms in one place to outperform firms elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 同一地点相互关联的企业整体胜过外地企业的能力
senses.example: The cluster's competitiveness attracted suppliers from three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个产业集群的竞争力吸引了三国的供应商。
senses.why: the unit can be a place rather than a company, because linked firms share suppliers and skills.
senses.whyCN: 计量单位可以是地点而非公司，因为相互关联的企业共享供应商与技能。

senses.title: Cost and price competitiveness
senses.definition: the ability to offer similar goods at a lower cost or price than rivals
senses.definitionCN: 以低于对手的成本或价格提供同类商品的能力
senses.example: Cheap energy gave the mills a cost competitiveness that lasted a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价能源给了这些工厂持续十年的成本竞争力。
senses.why: the phrase is often narrowed to price because the cheapest offer is the easiest advantage to measure.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法常被收窄到价格，因为最便宜的报价是最容易测量的优势。

senses.title: Strength built on productivity and innovation
senses.titleCN: 由生产率与创新支撑的竞争力
senses.definition: long-run competitive strength created by efficiency gains and new products rather than by cheap inputs
senses.definitionCN: 由效率提升与新产品而非廉价投入创造的长期竞争实力
senses.example: Innovation, not wage cuts, sustains long-run competitiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 维系长期竞争力的是创新，而非削减工资。
senses.why: economists separate this sense because cost advantage can vanish when prices or wages change.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这一义项单列，因为成本优势会随价格或工资变化而消失。

senses.title: Advantage from exchange rates and wages
senses.titleCN: 汇率与工资带来的优势
senses.definition: a temporary edge produced by currency movements or lower labour costs
senses.definitionCN: 由汇率变动或较低劳动成本造成的暂时优势
senses.example: A strong currency hurt the sector's competitiveness overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 本币走强一夜之间削弱了该行业的竞争力。
senses.why: in trade policy the word often names price effects that no firm controls.
senses.whyCN: 在贸易政策中，这个词常指企业无法左右的价格效应。

senses.title: A rank on a competitiveness index
senses.definition: a position in a published ranking that compares economies or industries
senses.definitionCN: 在比较经济体或产业的公开排名中的位置
senses.example: The economy moved up ten places in the competitiveness index.
senses.exampleCN: 该经济体在竞争力指数上上升了十位。
senses.why: once the concept was indexed, the noun came to mean a score as well as a capacity.
senses.whyCN: 当这一概念被编成指数，这个名词也指分数，而不只是能力。

senses.title: Relative strength in any contest
senses.titleCN: 任何争夺中的相对实力
senses.definition: the degree to which any side can hold its own against competitors
senses.definitionCN: 任何一方在与对手相争时能站稳的程度
senses.example: Both teams trained for months, and their competitiveness showed in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 两队都训练了数月，决赛里显出了各自的竞争力。
senses.why: detached from trade, the noun simply measures how well a side can fight for a share.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个名词只衡量一方争夺份额的实力。

intro.en: Competitiveness is an English-built noun: the Latin verb competere gives competitive through -ive, and the native suffix -ness turns that adjective into a quality. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitiveness 是英语自造的名词：拉丁动词 competere 经 -ive 构成 competitive，本族后缀 -ness 再把形容词变成性质名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Competere 'to seek together, strive jointly' joins com- 'together' to petere 'seek'. The rivalry sense was fixed in Latin before English borrowed it.
items.cn: competere「一起寻求、共同力争」把 com-「共同」接在 petere「寻求」上；相争义在英语借入前已在拉丁语中固定。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives of tendency, as in competitivus; French -if and English -ive continue that pattern.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示倾向的形容词，如 competitivus；法语 -if 与英语 -ive 延续了这一模式。

items.en: Competitive entered English in the seventeenth century as an adjective for things able to contend, and later for prices and markets.
items.cn: competitive 在 17 世纪进入英语，形容能够相争的事物，后来也用于价格与市场。

items.en: The native suffix -nes, now -ness, turned adjectives into nouns of quality, as in darkness and readiness; competitiveness is a regular formation.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -nes（今 -ness）把形容词变成性质名词，如 darkness、readiness；competitiveness 是规则的构成。

items.en: Competitiveness became a policy term in the late twentieth century, when reports began ranking nations and regions by it.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，随着报告开始据此给国家与地区排名，competitiveness 成为政策术语。

items.en: The exact first use of the noun is not recorded; nineteenth-century economics already used competitive in the modern sense. No step in the word chain is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词的最早用例没有确切记录；19 世纪经济学已在使用现代义的 competitive。词形链条各环节并无存疑之处。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same verb that answer a different question; group two holds related measures of performance that are not the same as the capacity itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个动词、却回答不同问题的词；第二组是相关的绩效指标，与「能力」本身并不等同。

entries.definition: The process or event of rivals striving; competitiveness is a capacity, while competition is the struggle in which it shows.
entries.definitionCN: 对手相争的过程或赛事；competitiveness 是一种能力，competition 是这种能力得以显现的斗争。

entries.tag: a skill not a market edge
entries.definition: From the 'be fit for' branch of competere: a specific skill or qualification a person or firm possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 competere 的「适合」一支：人或企业具备的具体技能或资格。

entries.definition: The adjective that competitiveness nominalises; it describes the side or price, not the abstract capacity.
entries.definitionCN: competitiveness 所名词化的形容词；它描述一方或价格，而非抽象能力。

entries.definition: The active participle, used for sides currently in the contest or for mutually exclusive claims.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，用于当前正在相争的各方，或相互排斥的主张。

entries.definition: The ratio of output to input in production; it is a source of competitiveness, not the same as the ability to sell.
entries.definitionCN: 生产中产出与投入的比率；它是竞争力的来源，但不等同于销售能力。

entries.definition: The use of the least resources for a result; a firm can be efficient yet fail to sell if demand is weak.
entries.definitionCN: 用最少资源取得结果；企业可以很高效，却在需求疲弱时卖不出去。

entries.definition: One favourable condition; competitiveness is the overall capacity that such conditions support.
entries.definitionCN: 某一项有利条件；competitiveness 是这些条件所支撑的总体能力。

entries.definition: How well a firm actually did in a period; it reports results, while competitiveness predicts what results are possible.
entries.definitionCN: 企业在一段时间内的实际表现；它汇报结果，而竞争力预测可能取得什么结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: competitive + -ness: the quality of being able to strive.
normal.cn: competitive + -ness：能够相争的性质。

normal.en: The family runs compete, competition, competitor, competitive, competitively, competitiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compete、competition、competitor、competitive、competitively、competitiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: international competitiveness, cost competitiveness, competitiveness index.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：国际竞争力、成本竞争力、竞争力指数。

normal.en: The word can be measured at three levels: firm, industry, country.
normal.cn: 这个词可在三个层面计量：企业、产业、国家。

normal.en: Its usual sources are productivity, innovation, skills and infrastructure.
normal.cn: 它的常见来源是生产率、创新、技能与基础设施。

abstract.en: Picture a rankings board where one name climbs a line each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一张排名板，同一个名字每年往上爬一行。

abstract.en: Picture a training log that grows thicker while the race times grow shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象训练记录越写越厚，而比赛用时越来越短。

abstract.en: Picture two factories on one river, one retooling while the other stands still.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条河边的两座工厂，一座在换设备，另一座原地不动。

examples.en: The report ranked the economy by competitiveness rather than by income.
examples.cn: 该报告按竞争力而非收入给经济体排名。

examples.en: Firms that ignore training slowly lose competitiveness.
examples.cn: 忽视培训的企业会慢慢失去竞争力。

examples.en: Currency swings can change competitiveness before any factory adjusts.
examples.cn: 汇率波动能在任何工厂作出调整之前改变竞争力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competitive（竞争）+ ness（性质）」——能在赛场上争一争的性质 → 竞争力

root: 拉丁 competere「一起寻求、共同力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）→ 拉丁 -ivus 构成 competitivus → 英语 competitive + 本族后缀 -ness。整词为英语自造的性质名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one capacity: a side can hold its own, and that capacity is then scaled from a firm to a country and a region, narrowed to costs, traced to productivity, tied to exchange rates, turned into a rank, and finally applied to any contest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种能力展开：一方能站稳脚跟，这种能力再从事企业放大到国家与区域、收窄到成本、追溯到生产率、联系到汇率、变成排名，最后用于任何竞赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a training log that thickens while the race times shorten.
core.cn: 核心意象：训练记录越写越厚，比赛用时越来越短。

branches.en: THE FIRM: the plain capacity of one business to win sales.
branches.cn: 企业：一家企业赢得销量的朴素能力。

branches.en: SCALED UP: the same capacity attributed to an economy or to a linked cluster.
branches.cn: 被放大：同一种能力被归给一个经济体或一个关联集群。

branches.en: PRICE AND CURRENCY: the cheapest offer, and the exchange-rate edge no firm controls.
branches.cn: 价格与汇率：最便宜的报价，以及企业无法左右的汇率优势。

branches.en: THE DURABLE BASE: productivity and innovation keep the capacity from evaporating.
branches.cn: 持久的基础：生产率与创新使这种能力不致蒸发。

branches.en: SCORE AND ANY CONTEST: a published rank, then the same capacity in a race or a debate.
branches.cn: 分数与任何竞赛：公开排名，以及赛跑或辩论中的同一种能力。

intro.en: The noun stacks a Latin verb, a Latin adjective suffix and a native English suffix, so each layer can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个名词叠了一个拉丁动词、一个拉丁形容词后缀与一个英语本族后缀，因此每一层都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin competere gives compete and competition, -ivus gives competitive, and Old English -nes gives competitiveness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 competere 提供 compete 与 competition，-ivus 提供 competitive，古英语 -nes 提供 competitiveness。
